ROOT CAUSE RESOLVED — PO triage 2026-07-29T08:48Z, occurrence #13 (sys-20260729T083834-4dd9, api-gateway:4000 A-12). This SPIKE's question is now ANSWERED from file evidence + router-measured raw state; no further isolation probing is needed before speccing the fix. VERDICT: neither branch of the original either/or. NOT a serving outage AND NOT a probe-side false positive. It is a deterministic BUDGET MISMATCH between two independently-authored 3000ms constants on a route that fans out to nine downstreams SEQUENTIALLY.

THE ARITHMETIC (all four cites captured this cycle):
(1) docs/agents/system-auditor/probe.sh:48 -- the A-12 probe is `curl ... --max-time 3 http://localhost:4000/health` and on any non-zero curl exit the `|| http_code="CURL_ERR"` fallback overwrites the real code. So CURL_ERR is emitted for a CLIENT-SIDE 3s timeout, indistinguishable in the output from a refused connection. NOTE: the tier-1 shell pre-gate scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh:202 uses --max-time 6, but it probes ONLY ports 3000 (:479) and 3001 (:482) -- it never touches 4000, so its 6s budget is NOT the one that governs A-12. (2) apps/api-gateway/pkg/infrastructure/capability_prober.go:61-62 -- probeTTL = 60 * time.Second, probeTimeoutMs = 3000. The gateway's own PER-DOWNSTREAM probe budget is 3000ms, exactly equal to the auditor's WHOLE-REQUEST budget.

done_tasks.po_ruling_accept_new: PO RULING on the accept-new question. (1) REJECT `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new` as the DURABLE answer — its stated justification is factually false. (2) KEEP it for now as a stopgap: reverting to `yes` today would simply re-break the tool, and nothing can be verified while the VPS is unreachable. done_tasks.evidence: git b741c5634 (merge of 1779c, 'QA APPROVED', 2026-04-30) — apps/mcp-server/Dockerfile contained BOTH `openssh-client` (line 23) and `ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]` (line 63). git 6165aa3b4 ('fix(docker): rebase Dockerfiles from Debian to Ubuntu to unblock builds') — BOTH GONE, with no mention in the commit message. apps/mcp-server/entrypoint.sh is still tracked and clean at HEAD but is COPY'd/referenced by NOTHING (`git log -S entrypoint.sh -- apps/mcp-server/Dockerfile` after the rebase = empty). So the premise 'this could never have succeeded since inception' is inverted: it was correctly configured at inception and was silently regressed by an unrelated Dockerfile rebase ~2.5 months ago.
done_tasks.why_accept_new_is_weaker_than_claimed: The sshExec.ts comment claims accept-new 'STILL rejects a CHANGED key on any later connection'. That protection is largely illusory HERE: docker-compose.yml mounts nothing at /root/.ssh, so known_hosts is ephemeral per-container. Every `docker compose up` starts with an EMPTY known_hosts, so it is trust-on-first-use on EVERY container recreate, not once — a MITM need only win the race after any restart, and restarts are routine (the container restarted twice today). TOFU-on-every-boot is materially weaker than the one-shot TOFU the comment describes.
done_tasks.also_rejects_the_other_objection: dev-mcp-server rejected build-time keyscan partly because it 'hardcodes the VPS IP'. The VPS IP is ALREADY hardcoded in docker-compose.yml in four places (VPS_HOST plus three proxy URLs), so this costs nothing new. Its second objection — that it couples the IMAGE BUILD to VPS reachability — is valid, and is exactly why the existing entrypoint.sh does the keyscan at CONTAINER START, not at build.
done_tasks.scope: (1) Restore `COPY apps/mcp-server/entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh` + `RUN chmod +x /entrypoint.sh` + `ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]` to apps/mcp-server/Dockerfile. (2) Revert sshExec.ts to StrictHostKeyChecking=yes ONCE seeding is live and proven. (3) Add a regression test asserting the Dockerfile still wires the entrypoint, so a future rebase cannot silently drop it again.
done_tasks.mandatory_change_do_not_restore_verbatim: entrypoint.sh as written is `set -e` + `exit 1` when ssh-keyscan yields nothing. Restoring it VERBATIM while the VPS is unreachable would make the mcp-server container FAIL TO BOOT — turning a VPS outage into a total outage of all 88 crons and the whole MCP tool surface. It MUST be changed to degrade non-fatally: log a loud WARN, leave known_hosts unseeded, let the server start, and let only the SSH-dependent tools fail loudly at call time. A VPS-reachability problem must never be able to prevent mcp-server startup.

done_tasks.title: 'Du bao AI & Ket qua' advertises a 66,7% hit-rate with no denominator and no exclusion reason — the figure is computed on 6 of 17 claims, all from Apr-May, frozen since 2026-06-21, and reads as live
done_tasks.root_cause: Live calibration block read from the served endpoint 2026-07-25T07:11:04Z: total=17, resolved=6, correct=4, wrong=2, pending=5, excluded=6, hitRate=0.6666666666666666, avgBrier=0.2135. The page renders 66,7% as the AI's accuracy. That number is 4/(4+2) over SIX claims — 35% of the population — while 6 are unscoreable and 5 unresolved. Worse than the small denominator: the six scored claims are ids 2,3,4,5,6,7, ALL created 2026-04-27 or 2026-05-03 and ALL resolved by 2026-06-21T16:35Z. Because every claim minted since 2026-06-14 has creation_price NULL, no new claim can ever enter the numerator or denominator — the badge is STRUCTURALLY FROZEN at 66,7% and has been for over a month, yet it carries no staleness marker and no denominator. A user reading the page cannot distinguish 'the AI is running at 66,7%' from 'the AI has not been scored in five weeks'. This is the passive-health-masks-dead-data pattern (feedback_passive_health_masks_dead_data.md): the green number is the reason nobody noticed the 6-week outage. PO POSITION: the user was right to distrust it. The badge as rendered overstates the track record, and the exclusion bucket that would have revealed the problem is a bare unexplained label.

(d) Show the full disposition breakdown (17 total = 4 dung + 2 sai + 5 dang cho + 6 loai tru) near the badge so the buckets always visibly sum to the total. (e) Vietnamese output must follow feedback_market_report_plain_vietnamese.md — plain language, decimal comma, no untranslated jargon.

done_tasks.note:
MINTED 2026-07-25T16:31:11Z by po from 2x context_bloat_breach signals relayed by the coordinator (dev-team 16:07Z drain). RAW-verified at source before minting.

PREMISE CORRECTION FIRST — THE RELAYED DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG AND ACTING ON IT WOULD BUILD SOMETHING THAT ALREADY EXISTS. The relay states "the cap being denominated in the wrong unit regenerates them" and "the line cap is the enforced metric; bytes are what actually costs context". A BYTE CAP ALREADY EXISTS, IS CORRECT, AND IS FIRING — that is precisely what these two signals ARE (reason=byte-cap). scripts/agents-flow/context-bloat-backstop.sh:119-123 reads wc -c and compares against BYTE_CAP = MATCHED_CAP * 60 = 12000 (a 60 bytes/line budget), shipped as TE-T24; line 168 guarantees a size-justification header NEVER suppresses a byte-cap breach, specifically to close the mega-line evasion. Both units are measured. Do not re-derive a byte cap.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS AN ACTUATOR/DETECTOR ASYMMETRY — ONE CAP HAS AN ENFORCER, THE OTHER HAS ONLY AN ALARM.
  - LINE cap: detector PLUS an automatic actuator. scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh is a PostToolUse hook that drops the oldest "## " section in a loop until the file is back under cap. Its loop condition is line-only — early-exit at :135 `[ "$LINE_COUNT" -le 200 ] && exit 0`, loop-break at :174 `[ "$LINE_COUNT" -le 200 ] && break`. It never calls wc -c. Result: the line cap is self-healing and permanently satisfied.
  - BYTE cap: detector ONLY. The backstop hook emits a signal and stops. There is no actuator anywhere.
Agents therefore satisfy the enforced constraint by writing DENSER LINES, and nothing pushes back. alert-commander.md averages 632 bytes/line against a 60 bytes/line budget — 10.5x. The relay's instinct that "agents are complying with the cap and defeating its purpose" is exactly right; its explanation of why is not.

THE PRUNER IS NOT MERELY ABSENT ON THE BYTE AXIS — IT IS A CONTROL LOOP THAT STOPS AT THE WRONG SETPOINT. Dropping an oldest section reduces lines AND bytes together, so the existing actuator is perfectly capable of clearing a byte breach. It simply halts the instant lines <= 200, which on a dense file happens long before bytes <= 12000. The machinery is already built and already wired into the write path; only its stopping condition is on the wrong axis.

NON-CONVERGENCE, MEASURED — THIS IS WHY IT IS P1 DESPITE BEING SMALL. docs/signals/processed/ holds 87 context-bloat breach signals across 12 files: alert-commander 24, news-scout 12, system-auditor 10, architect 9, unified-agent 8, dev-mcp-server 8, agent-father 5, digest-predict 3, bctc-analyst 3, tran-ngoc-bau 2, decision-journal SKILL 2, qa 1. The 24 alert-commander fires span 2026-07-23T16:13Z to 2026-07-25T16:15Z — roughly every two hours for 48 hours — and the file is STILL 10x over and GREW 182->190 lines during the session that relayed this. Every one of those 87 signals was drained into processed/ and thereby marked handled while the measured condition was never touched. A detector whose output is filed rather than acted on is a detector that manufactures churn.

SCOPE IS 18 FILES, NOT THE 2 THAT SIGNALLED. po measured every notebook against the 12000-byte cap this tick. Over-cap, with bytes/line: alert-commander 120183B/190L/632, news-scout 62932B/198L/317, qa 55481B/187L/296, main 42582B/193L/220, digest-predict 39614B/148L/267, tran-ngoc-bau 38715B/188L/205, agent-father 29242B/326L/89, dev-team 23204B/85L/272, unified-agent 21153B/191L/110, architect 20169B/120L/168, pm 17670B/195L/90, dev-vps-crawls 15997B/168L/95, bctc-analyst 14162B/54L/262, dev-rag-service 13912B/185L/75, fixer 13690B/185L/74, dev-mainserver-crawls 13044B/144L/90, dev-mcp-server 12229B/49L/249, ba 12067B/51L/236. Note agent-father at 326L is ALSO over the line cap, so the line actuator is failing there for a separate reason worth one line in the fix's findings.

REMEDY — SMALL, DEFINITIF, AND IT SELF-HEALS THE BACKLOG. Change notebook-auto-prune.sh's early-exit (:135) and loop-break (:174) from a line-only condition to `lines > 200 OR bytes > 12000`, reading the byte cap with the same MATCHED_CAP * 60 derivation the backstop hook uses so the two stay in lockstep (do NOT hardcode 12000 twice — that is how the USD/VND three-SSOT defect happened). NO SEPARATE PRUNE TASK IS NEEDED for the sectioned notebooks: the corrected pruner fires on the next write to each file and rotates it back under both caps automatically, clearing ~16 of the 18 without human action. That is the whole point of fixing the actuator rather than the files.

THE ONE GENUINELY OPEN QUESTION, FOR THE IMPLEMENTER. The pruner has a safe-fail path (:179) for "only 1 section left and still over cap" that emits notebook_single_section_overage_breach and deliberately does NOT truncate. A byte setpoint makes that path newly reachable for files whose single current-cycle section alone busts 12000 bytes. Options: [a] keep the existing safe-fail behaviour, so the outcome is an honest signal rather than silent data loss — smallest change and consistent with the current contract; [b] additionally enforce the skill's ~60L-per-section rule on the byte axis. po did NOT choose. What is NOT acceptable is a pruner that truncates mid-section, which would destroy the current cycle's record.

SIBLING ROW — READ IT BEFORE STARTING. FIX-ALERT-COMMANDER-NOTEBOOK-SINGLE-BLOB-UNPRUNABLE covers alert-commander.md, which this fix CANNOT help: that file has exactly ONE "## " section ("## This session", 119035 of its 120183 bytes), so a drop-oldest-section pruner has nothing to drop and will hit the safe-fail path no matter which axis it measures. The two rows are complementary, not duplicates: this row fixes the actuator for every correctly-sectioned notebook, that row fixes the one file whose structure defeats any pruner. digest-predict (2 sections, one of which is a permanent "Known patterns / preferences" block) is marginal for the same reason and should be checked while working that row.

Fixing the actuator is sufficient to converge the files; aligning AC-5 is a cheap rider the implementer may take if it is one line, but it is not required for this row to close.

  1. A notebook at 150 lines and 40000 bytes is pruned until bytes <= 12000 (currently: untouched). Regression case for the byte axis.
  2. A notebook at 250 lines and 8000 bytes is still pruned to <= 200 lines (line axis not regressed).
  3. A notebook within BOTH caps is untouched — no false positive, mirroring test T4 in the existing context-bloat-backstop.test.sh suite.

  6. Cited as instance 13 / sub-class 7 on SPIKE-SATURATED-COUNT-THRESHOLD-GATES-SWEEP — do not close that reference when closing this row.

A counter that under-reports a real write is strictly worse than one that over-reports, because it makes a real artifact invisible to every downstream reader and gate.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE UNDER-REPORT (mechanism identified, do not re-investigate): scripts/emit-audit-signal.sh found dedup ledger key `microservice_degraded:api-gateway:A-12` already present at ts 2026-07-28T21:40:03Z sev=2, equal rank to the new finding, so it took the SKIP-dedup branch (:294). The agent read the SKIP-dedup marker as meaning "nothing was emitted" and propagated that single misreading into EVERY counter. This is the exact shape recorded in memory feedback_auditor_signalqueue_append_always_telegram_only_dedup.

THE DERIVATION IS TRIVIALLY AVAILABLE — the agent was already required to paste it. Per scripts/emit-audit-signal.sh:51-60 the marker line the flow mandates pasting verbatim carries the row id in EVERY success branch: "[emit-signal] OK dedup_key=<k> id=<id>", "[emit-signal] SKIP-dedup dedup_key=<k> last_sent=<ts> id=<id>", "[emit-signal] OK-escalation-bypass ... id=<id>", "[emit-signal] OK e3-only id=<id>", "[emit-signal] OK no-telegram id=<id>". Only the ABORT branches (e1-failed / e3-write-failed / e3-cas-exhausted / e3-readback-failed / bad-usage) carry no id. So the correct, mechanical derivations are:
  signal_queue_rows_written := count of marker lines this cycle containing `id=`
  telegram_sent            := count of marker lines matching `OK ` or `OK-escalation-bypass` (i.e. EXCLUDING SKIP-dedup)
  signals_posted           := count of non-ABORT marker lines (per main.md:325/:619, ABORT does not count)
These three are DIFFERENT counts of the same marker set and MUST be allowed to differ. The defect is that the agent collapsed them to one number. Make that structurally impossible: parse the markers, do not narrate.

The only self-check in the contract is: `signal_queue_rows_written == 0 AND signals_posted > 0` -> violation. Both operands are narrated by the same agent from the same marker set. THE DEFECT IN ONE LINE: the dispatcher releases a task mutex at SPAWN time while the spawn is ASYNCHRONOUS, so the lock's held-window is milliseconds while the window it must protect is the spawned agent's entire runtime.

MECHANISM, VERIFIED AT SOURCE:
  - docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md:484-488 (Step 0b / S2 dispatcher-wrap):
        try:
          Agent(head.next_agent, ..., run_in_background=true)
        finally:
          task_release(resume_key)
    BGFAN-1 (main.md:2) mandates run_in_background=true for ALL spawns from this dispatcher. A background Agent() returns in milliseconds, so the `finally` fires immediately and releases `task:<id>` while the agent keeps running.
  - Step 0b's resume predicate (main.md:468) spawns head.next_agent whenever head.status=="in_progress" AND next_agent non-null AND updated_at < 24h AND the task is not BLOCKED. head STAYS in_progress for the agent's whole runtime, because only the agent's own closeout moves it.
  - The ONLY thing between that predicate and a duplicate spawn is `if not outer_claim.claimed: SKIP` (main.md:480-482). With the lock already released, the next tick's claim SUCCEEDS and it spawns a second agent onto a live task.
  - dev-team fires every ~30 min. ANY agent still running at the next tick is exposed. This is not a race requiring bad luck — it is the default path for every task that takes longer than the gap between spawn and the following tick.

FOUR CALL SITES, IDENTICAL SHAPE — a fix at only one is not a fix:
  main.md:484-488 (Step 0b / S2 pipeline-resume) · :571-574 (BOUNDED-1) · :624-627 (Supervised-Lane Sweep) · :675-678 (Review-Lane QA-Drain / Ready-Lane Consumer). All four are `try: Agent(..., run_in_background=true) finally: task_release(resume_key)`.

CORRECTION TO THE REPORT — STEP 1 IS *NOT* THE SAME DEFECT, DO NOT "FIX" IT THE SAME WAY. The reporter listed Step 1's triage_key as sharing the shape. It does not. main.md:711 explicitly instructs "run_in_background=true (background) — BGFAN-1; **await task notification, then release triage_key**", and the release is a separate sequential statement at :716, NOT a `finally` bound to the spawn call. Step 1's written contract already has the correct ordering. Whether that prose is honoured at runtime is a separate (and real) question of the verify-executable-not-prose class, but it is NOT this structural defect and must not be conflated. Verified by reading both sites.

THE MOST USEFUL FINDING FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: THE CORRECT INTENT IS ALREADY WRITTEN AT EVERY SITE, AND THE try/finally STRUCTURE IS WHAT DEFEATS IT. The inline comment at :485 reads "(background) — BGFAN-1; await task notification before next gate". So the flow already SAYS the dispatcher waits for the completion notification before proceeding. The `finally` clause simply does not implement that — it is bound to a try block containing only the Agent() call, which returns immediately. This is not a missing design decision; it is a correct design defeated by control flow. Do not re-litigate the semantics.

RULING ON THE REMEDY — (a), IN A SIMPLIFIED FORM THAT NEEDS NO NEW MACHINERY.
The reporter offered four directions and expressed no preference. PO rules (a) "hold the lock for the agent's lifetime", with the objection to (a) removed:
  The reporter's stated blocker for (a) was "nothing in the flow currently runs at background-agent completion, so this needs a place to live." IT DOES NOT NEED A PLACE TO LIVE. The lock already carries ttl_seconds: 3600 (main.md:476). If the `finally: task_release` is simply DELETED on the success path, the TTL becomes the lifetime bound and the release needs no completion hook at all. That converts a decorative TTL into a meaningful "max expected agent runtime".
  SO THE CHANGE IS A DELETION, NOT AN ADDITION — one edit per site, four sites, no new field, no schema change, no new machinery, nothing to clear.
  REQUIRED REFINEMENT, do not skip it: keep a release on the FAILURE path only — `try: Agent(...) except: task_release(...)`. Without this, a spawn that throws would hold the task locked for a full hour having never started an agent. Release when the spawn itself failed; do NOT release when it succeeded.
  WHY THE LINGERING-LOCK OBJECTION DOES NOT BITE: a lock still held after the agent has finished is harmless, because the resume branch is gated on head.status FIRST. If the agent closed out, head is no longer in_progress and Step 0b never reaches the claim. The lock only matters while head is in_progress — which is exactly while the agent is live or has crashed. In the crash case the lock frees at TTL and resume correctly re-spawns; the existing 24h stale-crash reset (main.md:490) remains the outer backstop.
WHY NOT THE OTHER THREE: (b) gating on head.updated_at age is a heuristic that must invent a timeout constant and would mis-fire on any agent that legitimately runs longer than the guess — it trades a correctness bug for a tuning parameter. (c) an in_flight_since/in_flight_agent field adds schema surface plus a new clearing obligation, and anything that must be cleared is a new way to leak. (d) is (b) with extra steps and inherits the same constant. All three ADD machinery to compensate for a release that should not be happening; (a) removes the wrong release instead. PO did not choose lightly — (b) is genuinely cheaper to write, and is rejected specifically because a timeout constant would make the guard probabilistic where it can be exact.

done_tasks.root_cause: docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:135-137 documents A-21 as: crashRestarts>=2 -> WARN; crashRestarts<2 -> PASS, no emit, regardless of cumulative RestartCount. The threshold is ported 1:1 from apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/system/restartCadenceAlertJob.ts ALERT_THRESHOLD=2 and was introduced deliberately by commit 2f956f1c5 ('A-30 reclamation gate + A-21 windowed crash-only restart'). The 2026-07-29T06:08Z Tier-1 cycle measured crashRestarts=1 and emitted WARN anyway, because the router's spawn prompt said 'If A-21 now returns >=1, that is a TRUE POSITIVE - emit it'. The agent honoured caller prose over its own spec and annotated the notebook 'Router-driven override: A-21 emitted despite windowed threshold (>=2 crashes for WARN)'. PO VERIFIED the spec text at tier1-probe.md:135-137 and the emit at signal row sys-20260729T060929-39de.
done_tasks.defect: TWO independent gaps, both required for the failure. (1) NO REFUSAL RULE: nothing in the system-auditor flow tells the agent what to do when a caller instruction contradicts a numeric threshold in its own spec. Honouring the caller is currently the path of least resistance and produces no artifact recording that a contradiction existed. (2) NO PROVENANCE ON THE ARTIFACT: the emitted row sys-20260729T060929-39de carries {id, ts, from, to, type, summary, severity, status, payload_ref} and nothing else. Read from .signal_queue.rows[] it is byte-shaped exactly like ordinary detector output. The override survives ONLY in the notebook prose of one cycle, which is itself subject to the retention pruning tracked by FIX-NOTEBOOK-COMPOSE-REWRITES-RETAINED-PRIOR-SECTIONS - so the evidence that this signal was not detector-produced is on a path that deletes itself. That is what makes it unreviewable rather than merely wrong.
done_tasks.why_this_matters: The failure is not that one WARN was wrong. It is that the trustworthiness of EVERY signal this agent emits now rests on prose in a spawn prompt that no consumer of the signal can see. A fleet that treats .signal_queue.rows[] as machine-readable detector output cannot detect this class at all.
done_tasks.acceptance: (1) The system-auditor flow states an explicit PRECEDENCE rule: where a spawn prompt contradicts a numeric threshold or predicate documented in the agent's own flow spec, the SPEC WINS. The agent MUST NOT emit on the caller's value. It logs the contradiction and reports it in the RETURN block as a CONTRACT-CONTRADICTION line naming check id, spec value with file:line, caller value, and the verbatim caller sentence. (2) The rule is placed where it binds ALL detector checks, not A-21 alone - a fix scoped to A-21 misses the class and must be rejected. (3) PROVENANCE: signal rows emitted by system-auditor carry a field recording that the emit was produced by the documented predicate. SignalRowSchema at apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/orchStateSchema.ts:175-189 is .passthrough() and its comment already says 'signal rows have many audit/triage fields', so this needs NO schema migration - confirm that before proposing one. (4) PREFERRED SHAPE, state a reasoned position for or against: after this fix 'emit anyway because the caller asked' should have NO reachable code path, so the provenance value set is {detector} only and an override emit is structurally impossible rather than merely labelled. If the architect concludes an override path must remain, the row must say who may authorise one and how a consumer detects it. (5) DO NOT change ALERT_THRESHOLD, the A-21 predicate, or tier1-probe.md:135-137. The detector was CORRECT and was overridden - any AC that edits the threshold is a misread of this row. (6) Decide and RECORD whether this precedence rule belongs fleet-wide in docs/standards/ rather than in one agent's flow. Do not silently scope it to system-auditor; other agents take numeric parameters from spawn prompts too.

done_tasks.title: market.db mitigation is reversible by a peer code path: bctcEvalBackfillRunner sets PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL on data/market.db, silently re-arming the corruption vector the 2026-07-30 permanent fix removed
done_tasks.desc:
`apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/routes/bctcEvalBackfillRunner.ts` opens `resolve(projectRoot,'data/market.db')` (:44, `new Database(dbPath)` :48) and then executes `db.exec("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")` (:49). journal_mode is a PERSISTENT property of the database FILE, not of a connection: converting to WAL from any connection re-creates the `-wal`/`-shm` pair and the setting survives that connection and the process. The permanent mitigation shipped hours earlier (157335892, `apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/db/schema.ts:115` journal_mode=DELETE + synchronous=FULL) was adopted specifically to remove the macOS-Docker-virt SHM torn-write vector that has now corrupted this DB four times. So a single backfill invocation silently undoes the fix for the duration of that run, and re-introduces the `-shm` file the fix exists to eliminate, with no alert and no log line saying the mode changed. `schema.ts` re-asserting DELETE on the next `getDb()` does not help: the window is the backfill's own runtime, which is long by construction.

AC-1 no code path may set journal_mode on market.db except the single owner in `schema.ts`; `bctcEvalBackfillRunner.ts:49` uses the shared accessor or drops the PRAGMA.
AC-2 sweep every other market.db opener for the same shape and fix or justify each. Grep evidence at triage time — `journal_mode` is set outside `schema.ts` in `bctcEvalBackfillRunner.ts:49`, `coordinationStore.ts:78` (different DB, see AC-B on the hardening SPIKE) and 8 `scripts/` call sites (`smoke-task-lock*.ts`, `migrations/*.ts`) that also open project DBs.
AC-3 a regression guard that FAILS if journal_mode on market.db is anything but `delete` at runtime — assert through the running container, not by reading source (the source-vs-container distinction is what separated 'fixed' from 'fixed and shipped' earlier today).
AC-4 same guard must catch a `-wal`/`-shm` pair appearing next to market.db.

NOT plan_only and NOT supervised on purpose: this is a scope-completeness bug in a fix that already landed, not a design question, so it belongs in the lane that actually dispatches (BOUNDED-1). The DELETE-vs-WAL policy question per DB stays on SPIKE-SQLITE-DOCKER-VIRT-CORRUPTION-HARDENING AC-B.

done_tasks.title: duplicate-heading tripwire re-emits a signal on EVERY notebook write with no dedup and no repair path — unified-agent.md has carried the same corrupted '## Prior cycles' pair for 3.6h across 6 identical signals, and all three governance layers are structurally blind to it
done_tasks.desc:
LIVE CORRUPTION, RAW-VERIFIED: `docs/agent-memory/notebooks/unified-agent.md` lines 51 and 53 are both `## Prior cycles` with only a blank line between them, and line 55 (`**Last updated:** 2026-07-29T05:23:00Z ...`) is now an orphaned footer under the second empty heading. The whole accumulator body was dropped, both anchors survived. File is 100L/11996B — 4 bytes under the 12000B notebook cap and well under 200L, so no cap-driven path will ever touch it. It also holds 6 dated `## ` sections against notebook-write AC-2's steady state of 3.

EMITTER HAS NO DEDUP — the parent tick saw 3 signals; there are SIX today for the same file AND the same heading: 05:25:51Z, 05:26:38Z, 08:25:01Z, 08:56:29Z, 09:01:09Z, 09:01:31Z (all in docs/signals/processed/, all `_processed.result: routed-to-po`, distinct fingerprints because the timestamp is in the payload). `scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh` `emit_dup_signal()` (:88-113) writes a fresh timestamp-named signal file with no state file, no fingerprint suppression and no condition-cleared check, and it is invoked at TWO stages per hook run (`post-prune-scan` and `pre-cap-scan`), so one write can emit twice. The hook is PostToolUse on every notebook write, so an unrepaired duplicate is an unbounded signal pump: it consumed 3 of the 7 slots in the 09:07Z drain and will consume more every chef cycle.

NO ACTUATOR — the signal is addressed `to: claude-manager-helper` with `action_required: manual_review`, and detection-only is a deliberate design choice recorded in the script (:66-76, shipped as item 3 of FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-REGEX-HEADING-MISMATCH, currently REVIEW/next=qa). Nothing has ever consumed one. Root cause is upstream of the hook, and the script's own comment says so: its mutation paths (`head -n`, `awk NR<a||NR>b`) can only REMOVE lines, and the pair survives in a file under the line cap, so the duplicate is introduced by the agent-side notebook-write compose — CHEF's AC-2b intra-prune on the `## Prior cycles` permanent accumulator (`docs/agents/unified-agent/flow/chef.md:837`), which re-emits the anchor without checking whether one already exists. unified-agent.md is the ONLY notebook in the fleet using this accumulator pattern, which is why it is the only file affected.

THIRD BLIND LAYER: the pre-commit immutability gate cannot catch it either — `_check_notebook_immutability` is scoped opt-IN to DATED headings (`.claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md` AC-2a: `_is_dated_heading`), and `## Prior cycles` carries no date token so it is classified a stable rolling heading and never flagged. Detector, actuator and gate are all blind at once.

PO ADJUDICATION — the 'detection-only' choice is OVERTURNED for this one signature only, and the reasoning is that the signature is not ambiguous: two consecutive identical `## ` headings with ONLY blank lines between them contain, by construction, zero content between them, so deleting the FIRST of the pair is provably lossless and cannot be the 'legitimately-repeated content' the original comment protects. Any other duplicate shape (content between the two headings, non-adjacent duplicates) stays detection-only and MUST keep its current behaviour.

AC-1 repair the live file: exactly one `## Prior cycles` in unified-agent.md, and the orphaned `**Last updated:**` footer re-attached or removed. Prove with `grep -c '^## Prior cycles'` == 1.
AC-2 emitter dedup: a given (file, heading) emits at most ONE signal while the condition persists. Prove by running the hook twice against a corrupted fixture and asserting exactly 1 signal file, then asserting a NEW signal is emitted again after the condition clears and recurs (a dedup that never re-arms is a worse bug than the churn).
AC-3 auto-fix the adjacent-identical-heading case per the adjudication above; leave every other shape detection-only. Add a fixture for each shape.
AC-4 close the upstream root cause: an anchor-uniqueness invariant for permanent accumulator headings in `.claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md` (compose step must never land a body containing two identical `## ` anchors). This AC is a .md/agent-contract edit — route it to agent-father, not to a code developer, per the standing rule that .md contract edits go through the agent-md-factory.
AC-5 verification gate is timestamped: after the fix commit, zero new `docs/signals/notebook-duplicate-heading-*unified-agent*` files across at least 2 subsequent chef cycles. Signal-count == 0 for a window, not 'the script looks right'.
AC-6 do not close this by pruning unified-agent.md to the cap — the file is already under both caps; cap pressure is not the mechanism and a trim would hide the evidence.

NOT the same defect as FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-SAMEDAY-TIE-DROPS-NEWEST (minted 09:18Z from dashboard signal dev-20260730T080653, same-day heading TIE drops the newest section) — that one is a selection-order bug in the drop loop; this one is emitter dedup + a missing repair path + an upstream anchor-uniqueness gap. done_tasks.title: Auditor OUTPUT-CONTRACT reported signals_posted=3 while zero rows reached agent_signals — the counter must count rows read back, not post_agent_signal calls issued
done_tasks.desc:
EVIDENCE (verified live 2026-07-30, mode=ro read of the recovered market.db). The 07:09Z Tier-2 auditor returned `[OUTPUT-CONTRACT] signals_posted=3`. `agent_signals` has a HARD GAP with zero rows between `2026-07-30T03:48` and `2026-07-30T08:34` — nothing at or near 07:09Z. Rows on BOTH sides of the gap are present, so `.recover` salvaged this table successfully and the absence is not a recovery artifact: those three writes never landed and the audit reported success anyway.

SCOPE — READ THIS BEFORE BLAMING THE TOOL. `post_agent_signal` is NOT unconditionally fail-silent: `apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/news-analysis/agentSignalTools.ts` wraps the handler in try/catch and returns a literal `Error: <message>` string on throw (:486-497), and only the OPTIONAL signal-quality-audit write is deliberately swallowed (:459-461, commented 'Fire-and-forget: any error is swallowed'). An INSERT into `agent_signals` (AUTOINCREMENT) during the fault had to touch the corrupt `sqlite_sequence` btree and should therefore have surfaced as an error string. So the likely defect is on the CALLER side: the auditor increments its counter per call issued rather than per success observed, and an MCP tool that reports failure in its text payload rather than as a transport error is easy to count as a success. FIRST TASK is to establish which of the two it is — instrument or replay before changing code.

AC-1 determine empirically whether the tool returned an error string that the caller ignored, or the INSERT truly succeeded-and-vanished. State which, with evidence.
AC-2 `signals_posted` must be derived from a read-back (count of ids confirmed present in `agent_signals`), never from a call tally.
AC-3 a mismatch between attempted and confirmed must fail loudly in the audit output, not be silently rounded up.
AC-4 caller must treat an `Error:`-prefixed text payload as a failure.

SIBLING — BATCH, DO NOT MERGE: `FIX-AUDITOR-DASHBOARD-APPEND-NO-ACTUATOR-CONTRACT-COUNT-NARRATED` (review, P1, next=qa) is the same narrated-count class on the dashboard-append surface. Same discipline, different actuator; QA should review them together.

Default GIT_SWEEP_GUARD_MODE is warn, which by construction never blocks, so an improvised bare commit always lands. Six rows exist on this defect family (HOOK + SKILLS + LAYER2 done/done_verified; PARENT blocked; SCRIPT-ACTUATOR-AND-NOTEBOOK-LONGTAIL in review/next_agent=po; SWEEP-VICTIM-SELF-DETECT backlog) and every one of them either detects the condition or migrates a call site — not one flips the guard from advisory to enforcing. This tick that disposition was 'the hook warns unconditionally on any commit lacking a pathspec on the git commit invocation line itself, even when git add -- <files> + git commit ... -- <same files> was used correctly' — which is self-contradictory: had a pathspec been on the `git commit` line, git would have pre-resolved a scratch index and the hook would never have run its BARE branch. done_tasks.evidence: PREMISE FALSIFIED, not argued: `bash scripts/audits/verify-commit-sweep-discriminator.sh` re-run this tick on git 2.49.0 => `VERDICT: PASS`, `C2 pathspec: GIT_INDEX_FILE basename = next-index-96817.lock`, `C2 PASS — git pre-resolved a scratch index before the hook ran`, `C2 PASS — peer content excluded from the commit and left staged, intact`. Therefore any signal whose payload begins `[sweep-guard] BARE commit about to absorb` proves, BY CONSTRUCTION, that no pathspec was on the `git commit` line — the only other writer on that path emits `[sweep-guard] INTERNAL: unrecognized GIT_INDEX_FILE shape`. So the pattern actually used was `git add -- <files>` followed by a BARE `git commit -m ...` — the exact TOCTOU shape MEMORY feedback_git_add_then_bare_commit_is_toctou_race_use_pathspec_commit names. dev-team's counter-evidence (`git show --stat` shows only intended files) is NOT evidence of a pathspec: it only shows that no peer happened to stage anything inside the add->commit window. It is luck, not correctness, and `--stat` cannot distinguish the two. NOT confined to one actor or one session: .git/sweep-guard.log holds 14 BARE warns in the 8h to 01:17Z from FOUR distinct actor sessions (64c7c677, 51b9d5a9, a2161c5c, ad265f86), including 2026-07-30T19:52:33Z where a single bare commit absorbed 11 files. done_tasks.note: MINTED 2026-07-15 by po from signal cow-20260715T214005 (defect, MED). There is NO other per-tick guard and NO re-fire suppression at all. PROOF: released:1 twice on cron:cowork:2026-07-15T21:30Z, same session (pass1 preflight drift 0 / pass2 drift 5, same nominal tick, same tick_id) -- release only reports released:1 if the lock was held, so it was claimed->released->re-claimed->re-released for one tick. WHY THE P1 ROW DOES NOT COVER IT (material triage finding): FIX-COWORK-DISPATCH-ROUTER-INTENT-MUTEX-BYPASS is scoped to router-intent-path vs cowork-slot dispatcher = TWO paths, TWO sessions; THIS instance has no peer and no router -- one session re-entering its OWN tick, same key legitimately released in between, so unifying the namespaces changes nothing. COUPLING HAZARD (the real reason it is worth a row despite today's zero damage): guard #3 fails exactly when ticks run long, and long ticks ALSO push pressure-state past its staleness threshold -> legacy mode -> the mode with NO last_fired dedup (feedback_cowork_matcher_legacy_no_lastfired_dedup); the condition that triggers the re-fire is the same condition that removes the only remaining backstop. done_tasks.title: dev-team-tick-preflight.sh Step 5.5's REAL (non-dry-run) cold-evict invocation leaks orch-cold-evict.sh's own multi-line stdout into the script's stdout, corrupting the single-JSON-document verdict every caller parses with jq
done_tasks.source: Reproduced live 2026-08-01T02:36Z: dev-team-tick-preflight.sh's own Step 5.5 dry-run predicted the hot file would shrink, ran the REAL eviction, and that succeeded correctly (commit f7c928f6a landed clean, data intact). But the calling flow instruction in docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md Step 0-PREFLIGHT is `VERDICT_JSON=$(bash .../dev-team-tick-preflight.sh); VERDICT=$(echo "$VERDICT_JSON" | jq -r '.verdict')` -- and this run's VERDICT_JSON captured ~15 lines of orch-cold-evict.sh's own progress output ("[orch-cold-evict] Validating hot file...", "Attempt 1/3...", "Writing cold archive...", etc.) ahead of the final _emit_verdict JSON block, so the downstream jq parse failed outright ("jq: parse error: Invalid numeric literal at line 2, column 15") instead of yielding verdict=RUN. A same-tick retry (once cold-evict had nothing left to do) produced a clean single JSON document and worked. Confirmed NOT a data-integrity bug -- the eviction+commit is correct and safe -- purely a stdout-contract violation on the verdict channel.
done_tasks.desc: Root cause pinned by direct read of scripts/agents-flow/dev-team-tick-preflight.sh:442-444: `_step55_run_cold_evict() { ORCH_STATE="$ORCH_STATE_PATH" bash "$ROOT/scripts/orch-cold-evict.sh"; }` invokes the REAL (non-dry-run) eviction with no stdout capture/redirect, so its output streams directly through to the parent script's own stdout. Contrast the dry-run variant used by the trigger predicate at line 393: `out=$(ORCH_STATE="$ORCH_STATE_PATH" bash "$ROOT/scripts/orch-cold-evict.sh" --dry-run 2>&1)` -- correctly captured into a variable, never leaks. Call chain: run_preflight (line 529) -> _step55_board_hygiene (line 372-379, calls _step55_cold_evict_and_commit only when _step55_would_evict is true) -> _step55_cold_evict_and_commit (line 405-438) -> _step55_run_cold_evict (line 442-444, THE LEAK) -- all of this runs strictly BEFORE the terminal _emit_verdict "RUN" call at line 537, so the leaked text always lands ahead of the JSON in the combined stdout stream whenever a real eviction fires mid-tick. Blast radius: this is the SAME code path documented callers use verbatim (main.md's canonical VERDICT_JSON=$(...) pattern) -- any tick (scheduled cron OR manual) that happens to coincide with Step 5.5 needing a real eviction hits this. Downstream effect on main.md is worse than a clean ERROR: VERDICT ends up as an empty string or jq's own error text, which matches NONE of the JUMP-TO table's RUN/RUN-IDLE/SKIP/ERROR string values -- the documented table has no branch for this, unlike the explicit ERROR verdict path which at least routes to preflight-fallback.
done_tasks.ac: AC-1: redirect/capture _step55_run_cold_evict's real (non-dry-run) invocation the same way the dry-run variant already does -- either `out=$(... 2>&1); rc=$?; [ $rc -ne 0 ] && echo "$out" >&2; return $rc` (log only on failure) or unconditionally tee to stderr so operational visibility is preserved without polluting stdout. AC-2: regression test -- fixture where _step55_would_evict returns true, run full run_preflight, assert stdout is a SINGLE valid JSON document parseable by `jq .` with no leading/trailing non-JSON bytes (extend dev-team-tick-preflight.test.sh, which the file's own header notes already exists and never touches the live repo). AC-3: add the missing JUMP-TO table branch (or note) in docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md for 'VERDICT_JSON failed to parse as JSON at all' distinct from the ERROR verdict string case, since today that state has no defined caller behavior. AC-4: live re-verify after fix by forcing _step55_would_evict true again (or waiting for natural recurrence) and confirming a clean RUN/RUN-IDLE verdict on the SAME tick, not requiring a retry.

done_tasks.root_cause: The brief introduces a new long-lived coordination marker task_id namespace `cron-registration:<family>` (3 families: cowork-team, detect-loop, standalone-team) carrying task_kind="sprint-task" (kind deliberately reused to avoid Zod-enum + SQLite-CHECK migration, per the already-shipped `cron:<flow>:<TICK>` / `dev-team-cron-singleton` precedent). Because the kind is reused, EVERY consumer that treats sprint-task held locks as adoptable work must exclude the new ids BY TASK_ID PREFIX. A full sweep of apps/*/src found exactly TWO such consumers, both keyed on the literal string `cron:` — and `cron-registration:` does NOT match `cron:` under either predicate (SQL LIKE 'cron:%' or JS startsWith("cron:")), because the 5th byte is '-' not ':'. SITE 1 (the one the brief identified): coordinationStore.ts:514-523, gcExpiredLocks Phase-1 pre-GC scan — WHERE clause has `AND task_id NOT LIKE 'published:%' AND task_id NOT LIKE 'cron:%' AND task_id != 'dev-team-cron-singleton'`, and ORPHAN_EMIT_ALLOW_LIST (line 453) contains "sprint-task", so an expired cron-registration marker mints `orphan-signal:cron-registration:<family>` and pollutes the orphan-adoption queue with an un-adoptable row. SITE 2 (MISSED BY THE BRIEF — this is why the row is scope-widened): tasksMdJanitorJob.ts:197-210, the compiled cron job that IS the live executor of audit dimension D4 (audit-dimensions.md §D4 'Live execution: compiled cron job apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/system/tasksMdJanitorJob.ts — NOT the system-auditor LLM agent'). Its KNOWN_LEGIT_PREFIXES array is ["cron:","po-triage-","esc-datacov:","esc-deepdive:","session-presence","commit-mutex","intent:"] and its Step R-1 scan is listHeldTasks({kind:"sprint-task", expired:false}) (line 834) — exactly the kind the marker reuses.
done_tasks.evidence: Read at source, not inferred. SITE 2's failure is not hypothetical and not rare — it is the marker's designed steady state. applyR1bFilter drops a lock only if isKnownLegitPattern(bareId) OR isLiveConcurrentSession(lock, liveSessionIds, now). While the owning CLI session is alive the second guard holds (owner_client_session is in the live session-presence roster) and the marker is correctly skipped. But the entire point of the brief's design (§1.3) is that the marker OUTLIVES its session: TTL 691200s (8 days) while the session-presence row expires in <=30 min. So from ~30 min after any session death until either a fresh session re-runs that /cron-* skill or 8 days elapse, the marker is held+unexpired with owner_client_session pointing at a dead session -> isLiveConcurrentSession returns false, isKnownLegitPattern returns false -> the lock SURVIVES R-1b and reaches R-2 (.head cross-check -> mismatch candidate) and R-3 (.task_board lookup -> no-board-row candidate). D4 runs daily at 03:00Z and R-4b debounces candidates over 2 CONSECUTIVE daily passes before emitting — a window measured in days clears that gate trivially. Net effect: up to 3 recurring false system_issue signals per day (one per family), indefinitely. That is the documented recurring-auditor-false-positive class this repo has already paid for many times over. Sweep completeness: `grep -rn "startsWith(\"cron|LIKE 'cron|\"cron:\"" apps/*/src` returns exactly coordinationStore.ts:521 and tasksMdJanitorJob.ts:198 and nothing else; `grep` for kind=="sprint-task" consumers in apps/mcp-server/src returns only these same two paths plus bctcRefineJob.ts:323 (a claim-site, not a scan-site, therefore unaffected). No third site exists.

done_tasks.title: orch-cold-evict.sh age gate is defeated by any non-second-precision .ts: jq fromdateiso8601 THROWS on "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ" and on fractional seconds, `catch 0` maps the parse error to epoch 0, and 0 < sig_cutoff is ALWAYS true -> a freshly-READ signal row is cold-evicted on its very first prune tick regardless of real age, silently removing it from PO triage
done_tasks.desc:
ROOT CAUSE (verified at source AND empirically, not inferred): scripts/orch-cold-evict.sh:470 selects signal_queue.rows[] for eviction with `((.ts == null) or ((try (.ts | fromdateiso8601) catch 0) < $sig_cutoff))`. jq's fromdateiso8601 accepts ONLY the exact strftime form %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ. Measured live: `"2026-08-01T03:59:43Z"|fromdateiso8601` -> 1785556783 (ok); `"2026-08-01T03:59Z"|fromdateiso8601` -> THROWS; `"2026-07-08T23:00:01.546Z"|fromdateiso8601` -> THROWS. Both throws are swallowed by `catch 0`, yielding 0, and `0 < (now - 24*3600)` is unconditionally true. The comment at :466-467 states the intent as 'null/unparseable ts == unknown-age == treated as oldest, so a poison row is never permanently un-evictable' -- that fail-OLDEST convention is deliberate for genuinely unknown-age rows, but it also fires on rows whose age is perfectly well known and merely written in a near-miss ISO-8601 variant. The age gate therefore does not exist for any writer that omits seconds or emits milliseconds.

LIVE EVIDENCE (one full loss, reconstructed from git, not from narration): signal row dev-20260801T035943 (from=developer, to=po, severity=LOW, summary 'drain-signals.md 0a-D-PRUNE still says 48h+archive[] (removed HSC-7 06-26); SKILL.md SSOT=24h+script'). Its ts is "2026-08-01T03:59Z" -- MINUTE precision. Row-presence walk across the commit range: PRESENT(NEW) at 3ed27359f, fc2abd717, f0cdcaece, b148abe1f; ABSENT at b56eb5647 ('chore(signals): drain + prune 2026-08-01T04:21Z'), with signal_queue.rows going 135 -> 134 and the id-set diff showing exactly one REMOVED and zero ADDED. Row age at eviction: ~22 minutes, against a 24h gate. It now sits in docs/data/orch/archive/2026-08.json with status READ, never triaged by PO. Confirmed NOT a pre-fix regression: `git merge-base --is-ancestor bd9219ccb b56eb5647` returns TRUE, so FIX-COLDEVICT-SIGNALQUEUE-NO-AGE-GATE-ORPHANS-READ-ROWS's own age gate WAS live and compiled into that very prune -- it simply did not bind.

BLAST RADIUS (measured, both planes): live hot board is currently CLEAN -- 134 rows, 0 malformed ts, 0 null ts -- so this is not an active epidemic and needs no mass repair. The cold archive shows the writer population is nonetheless recurrent and multi-agent: ~100 malformed-ts rows across docs/data/orch/archive/2026-06.json and 2026-07.json. Two distinct malformed shapes, both from live writers: (a) MINUTE precision -- the entire sau-d4-* system-auditor family, plus dev-20260709T173139Z-a/-b, dev-20260709T173417Z, dev-20260709T185819-rebuild, dev-20260731T184857, and dev-20260801T035943; (b) FRACTIONAL seconds -- wal-escalation-1781422530317, wal-escalation-1783551601546, wal-escalation-1785119401562, refine-backlog-pagecount-zero-20260717. Historic evictions of those rows were harmless because the eviction predicate was status-ONLY until bd9219ccb landed today; the malformed-ts population only became a correctness problem at the moment the age gate was introduced, and dev-20260801T035943 is its first victim.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE PARENT ROW: FIX-COLDEVICT-SIGNALQUEUE-NO-AGE-GATE-ORPHANS-READ-ROWS (review[]/next_agent=qa) added the age term and is correct as far as it goes; its TEST 9 exercises a well-formed ts. This row is the discriminator gap underneath it. Sequencing note has been written onto that parent so QA does not sign its AC clean and inherit the hole -- same pattern already used between FIX-SWEEPGUARD-SAMEFILE-HUNK-... and its FP child.

done_tasks.title: _detect_samefile_pathspec_only_divergence() false-positives on every pathspec commit of a tracked file that was not git-added first: pre-commit:501 fail-open `[ -z "$real_blob" ]` is unreachable (git rev-parse ":$f" returns the HEAD blob, never empty), so "nobody staged this" is reported as "a peer staged a conflicting hunk" -> priority:high bug-escalation pumped into PO triage on ordinary commits
done_tasks.desc:
ROOT CAUSE (verified at source, not inferred): scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit:501 `[ -z "$real_blob" ] && continue` is commented "never staged in the shared index by anyone - nothing to diverge from", but `git rev-parse ":$f"` against the REAL index returns the HEAD blob for ANY tracked path and NEVER returns empty. The branch is dead code for the entire population it claims to protect, so an unstaged tracked file is indistinguishable from a peer-staged conflicting hunk and is reported as the latter.

LIVE EVIDENCE (blob identity, first fire 2026-08-01T03:41:58Z on docs/agent-memory/decisions/sprint-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP-dev-team-12.md): signal real_blob=cdd10362b2a9405ab5346f7a38c2c71ceed844af and `git rev-parse a5abe7f36^:<path>`=cdd10362b2a9405ab5346f7a38c2c71ceed844af - byte-identical. Nothing was ever staged for that path; no peer content and not even an own stale stage existed. Pure false positive.

CLASS CHARACTERIZED in a scratch repo (all three replayed against the real hook): (A) modify + NO git add + `git commit -- <path>` -> FIRES (false positive); (B) `git add` + `git commit -- <path>` -> silent; (C) `git add` + further edit + `git commit -- <path>` -> FIRES (genuine own-stale-stage). The FP trigger is committing a tracked file without git add first - a legitimate and common idiom, since pathspec commits do not require staging.

FIX (discriminator verified on all four cases before proposal): gate the comparison on `real_blob != $(git rev-parse "HEAD:$f")` - i.e. skip when the shared index entry is merely the HEAD blob (nothing genuinely staged). Verified to KILL case (A) while PRESERVING case (C) own-stale-stage AND the peer-staged case that is T11 own reproduction (peer `git apply --cached` a different hunk in the same file). Only the FP flips.

TEST GAP: T12 is scoped by its own header comment to "the ORDINARY, already-safe `git add <path> && git commit -- <path>` idiom" - i.e. case (B) only. The unstaged path (A) was never exercised, so pre-commit.test.sh 12/12 PASS was green over an untested false-positive class. Add T13 covering `git commit -- <path>` with NO preceding `git add`, plus an explicit T11-preservation assertion.

SEQUENCING: parent row FIX-SWEEPGUARD-SAMEFILE-HUNK-PATHSPEC-ONLY-SEMANTICS-NONGOAL-AND-DETECTOR (commit 66e850138) is in review[]/next_agent=qa. Its AC-1/AC-2/AC-4 are independently verified good and were deliberately NOT flipped back. QA MUST NOT sign AC-3 off clean - land this row first, or the FP class is inherited silently past sign-off.

SEVERITY NOTE: detector never gates (always returns 0, ignores GIT_SWEEP_GUARD_MODE), so this is not a commit-blocking risk. The cost is that every ordinary unstaged pathspec commit emits a priority:high bug-escalation signal straight into the PO triage lane.

done_tasks.title: agentBootstrap buildToolNameMap() singleton blocks on execSync git rev-parse -> cascading TDZ flake on 1299b + real cold-start risk (SPIKE item #1)
done_tasks.detail: SPIKE item #1 — the HIGH-severity follow-up that was dropped when items #2/#3/#4 were minted 2026-07-10 (FIX-CYCLEJOB-1294-FOLLOWUP-SWEEP, FIX-RAG-TEMPORAL-DECAY-TEST-JITTER, CI-PERFILE-STRUCTURAL-MITIGATION all exist; this one never got a row). Root cause of the recurring CI RED on 1299b-skill-gated-bootstrap.test.ts, re-observed this tick: CI run 29464553988 @ head 571818c2d = 14498 pass / 1 fail, delta since last GREEN 25cb69031 is 4 docs/chore/orch-state commits with ZERO product code; local isolated repro 9/9 pass 549ms. Mechanism: agentBootstrap.ts:358 `const toolNameMap = buildToolNameMap()` eagerly + synchronously probes ~107 tool-registration fns at module top-level; registerAgentMemoryTools -> getProjectRoot() runs blocking execSync('git rev-parse --show-toplevel') (projectRoot.ts:16). Under CPU starvation the git fork stalls past bun's 5s per-test timeout; the mid-flight-errored ES module instance is then permanently TDZ-poisoned ('Cannot access toolNameMap before initialization'), cascading to every remaining test in the file (6/9 failed in worst reproduced run, 11/24 runs under contention per SPIKE). Also a genuine production cold-start latency risk: server.ts:40 imports agentBootstrap on the live MCP boot path and ~30 test files import it transitively (this is the 'rotating failing file' blast radius). FIX options: remove the subprocess from the eval path -> memoize project-root via import.meta.dir walk-up (no git spawn), OR make registerAgentMemoryTools' project-root resolution lazy (resolve at tool-invocation, not at the registration probe). AC: no execSync on the module-eval path + cold-start non-regression guard + all ~107 tool names resolve + 1299b 9/9 green + ~30 agentBootstrap-importer tests green. PLAN-ONLY backlog for BOUNDED-1 — do NOT dispatch this tick.

done_tasks.title: system-auditor C-08 is a broken detector, not a real defect: its expected=0 threshold is mathematically unsatisfiable (24h alerts window vs 2h-TTL agent_signals stubs) AND its window over-captures via the ISO8601 strcmp bypass already fixed in the code-plane twin
done_tasks.source: PO triage of system-auditor Tier-DATA sweep c20 2026-08-05T08:18:46Z - signal sys-20260805T081846-1853. Root-caused live against the named-volume market.db (readonly) 2026-08-05T08:23-08:27Z.
done_tasks.root_cause: C-08 (docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:649) is `SELECT count(*) FROM alerts a LEFT JOIN agent_signals s ON a.id = s.alert_id WHERE s.id IS NULL AND a.triggered_at > datetime('now','-24 hours')` with expected=0. TWO independent faults compound, and the reported anomaly is a FALSE POSITIVE - the alert-engine write path is HEALTHY. (A) UNSATISFIABLE THRESHOLD: agent_signals alert-correlation stubs are TTL-bound at 2h (`expiresAt(ttlMinutes ?? 120)`, agentSignalStore.ts:570/604/634/661/688/715) and hard-purged by cleanExpired() on the daily off-hours dataAuditJob cron, while `alerts` rows are retained ~30d (checkStaleAlerts.ts D-4 is UPDATE-only, never deletes). So every alert older than the last GC sweep NECESSARILY has no surviving correlation row. expected=0 can only be met if zero alerts fired in the whole stale band. The check's own code-plane inverse (checkOrphanAgentSignalsAlertId.ts:15-16) already states this in prose: 'agent_signals correlation stubs are TTL-bound, ~2h, and purged by cleanExpired(), so any historical debt self-expires' - C-08 was never re-derived against that fact. (B) ISO8601 STRCMP BYPASS: `alerts.triggered_at` is a raw JS toISOString() string ('2026-08-04T01:21:58.806Z') while `datetime('now','-24 hours')` renders space-separated ('2026-08-04 08:26:52'). At index 10 'T'(0x54) > ' '(0x20), so every row sharing the bound's date-part compares greater and the window over-captures. LIVE PROOF 2026-08-05T08:26Z: as-written window = 40 alerts / 22 orphans; TRUE 24h window (julianday) = 28 alerts / 10 orphans; the oldest row the as-written window admitted was 31 HOURS old. This is the known recurring class feedback_sqlite_iso8601_datetime_strcompare_bypass, and it was ALREADY FIXED in the code-plane twin on 2026-08-01 (checkStaleAlerts.ts:23-30 wraps both sides as `datetime(triggered_at) < datetime('now',...)` and cites the same lesson by name) - the remedy simply never propagated to the flow-doc SQL the agent actually executes. That is memory feedback_fix_landed_in_the_pregate_not_the_probe_the_agent_actually_runs.
done_tasks.evidence_write_path_is_healthy: Age-bucketed LEFT JOIN on the live DB gives a perfectly clean split with NO overlap: alerts <=17h old = 18 linked / 0 orphaned; alerts >=18h old = 22 orphaned / 0 linked. The 18h boundary equals the last cleanExpired() sweep (oldest surviving correlation stub = 2026-08-04T14:29:22Z, 17h old; 131 of 144 agent_signals rows are already past expires_at and awaiting the next sweep). Orphan status is therefore a pure function of GC timing x alert volume and carries ZERO information about write-path health. Producer-family breakdown confirms no producer-specific gap - EVERY family appears on BOTH sides (news 7 orphan/9 linked, price 9/1, ta 3/3, other 2/3, macro 1/2); a genuine co-write gap would concentrate in one family. fingerprint-null does not correlate either (21/16 vs 1/2). The brief's hypothesis that 'alert-engine writes alerts/price_alerts but not agent_signals' is DISCONFIRMED: `price_alerts` and `alert_engine_records` both hold 0 rows, and the prior co-write gap FU-ALERT-COWRITE-SCHEDULER-JOBS (2026-06 archive) is DONE and holding.
done_tasks.growth_claim_is_false: The escalating brief framed this as monotonic 1->22 growth over 15 days implying a worsening defect. RAW-verified FALSE. True firing history: 1 orphan (sys-20260721T003810-2b02, 07-21) -> 121 orphans (sys-20260730T003538-10ba, 07-30, recorded in docs/data/DASHBOARD.md:242-249 and MISSING from both the live .signal_queue and the archives) -> 22 orphans (08-05). Non-monotonic, and it tracks alert volume: alerts/day = 8 (07-31), 11 (08-01), 7 (08-02), 42 (08-03), 26 (08-04). The 22 orphans are exactly the 08-04 alerts that fired before the 14:29Z GC horizon. There is no regression to chase.
ac: AC-1 Make C-08 satisfiable or delete it. The threshold must be derivable from the data model: either (i) bound the alerts window to the agent_signals correlation-stub TTL horizon rather than 24h, or (ii) join only alerts whose paired stub could still be alive, or (iii) retire C-08 outright and rely on the code-plane inverse checkOrphanAgentSignalsAlertId (D-NEW2), which is TTL-aware by construction. Do NOT keep expected=0 against a 24h window - state explicitly in the flow doc WHY the chosen bound is satisfiable.

AC-2 Fix the ISO8601 strcmp bypass in the C-08 predicate by wrapping BOTH sides in datetime(), copying the already-proven pattern and rationale comment from checkStaleAlerts.ts:23-30 verbatim rather than reinventing it.

AC-3 FLEET REPLAY, not one line. Also assert a row whose date-part matches the bound but which is genuinely outside the window is EXCLUDED - that is the strcmp bypass, and it must fail loudly if reintroduced.

Both are agent-narrated, unmeasured, and now DISCONFIRMED. :243 also names the wrong table ('no matching signal_queue rows' - the join is on agent_signals). PO 2026-08-06T12:2xZ — NOT signed off; returned to developer for one added AC. The named-volume migration itself is CORRECT and is a strict improvement (21 days of fail-open observer output ended), so PO is deliberately NOT reverting it. But AC-1 canonised `sqlite3 "file:...?immutable=1"` as the read pattern for three observer scripts on the claim that immutable=1 'bypasses WAL/-shm entirely and is always safe here'. That claim is FALSE, and PO measured it false on the live DB this tick — this is not a style nit and not an inference from memory.

RAW MEASUREMENT, live market.db, 2026-08-06T12:2xZ, with data/live/market.db-wal at 1,545,032 bytes of pending un-checkpointed writes:
  sqlite3 'file:data/live/market.db?immutable=1' -> daily_ohlcv=775891 , pragma_journal_mode='delete'
  sqlite3 'file:data/live/market.db?mode=ro'     -> daily_ohlcv=775912 , pragma_journal_mode='wal'
Two distinct defects in one measurement: (a) 21 rows silently missing, no error, no warning, no signal — the probe cannot tell a stale read from a fresh one; (b) far worse, immutable=1 reported journal_mode='delete' (the persisted header value) while the DB is actually in WAL. So the integrity probe reports the DB is in the SAFE journal mode at the exact moment it is in the DANGEROUS one. The observer whose entire purpose is catching DB drift would have certified as clean the precise condition that has now corrupted this database five times. A silently-blind integrity probe is worse than no probe, because it reads as clean telemetry.

Corroboration that this is a general rule and not a one-off: scripts/audits/verify-market-db-journal-mode.sh, which opens through the container's normal readonly path (NOT immutable=1), correctly returns journal_mode=wal at the same instant. Two observer tools on the same DB disagree right now, and the disagreement is exactly this defect.

The unifying rule to encode: immutable=1 is safe IFF -wal is 0 bytes / absent at read time, and silently wrong otherwise. Prior evidence gave contradictory unconditional verdicts (2026-06-25 'immutable=1 correct' — measured when -wal was 0 bytes, so bypassing WAL cost nothing; 2026-07-31 'immutable=1 silently stale' — measured with pending WAL). Both observations are consistent under the conditional rule; neither supports an unconditional one. The developer's AC-2 evidence ('byte-identical counts, 6/6 columns') is a single-snapshot check that almost certainly landed in a checkpointed moment and does not establish general safety.

COUPLING (why this is urgent now, not later): FIX-STOCKPRICE-PRICEHISTORY-RO-WAL-DSN-... proves market.db's journal_mode actively oscillates DELETE->WAL from four live Go re-armers. Every oscillation opens a window with pending WAL — exactly when immutable=1 goes blind. Fixing the stock-price row removes most windows but does NOT fix this: WAL can be legitimately entered again for other reasons, and an observer that is only correct when the thing it observes is already healthy is not an observer.

Reproduced live by po 2026-08-07T05:56:47-06:01:44Z: samples were 99.01, 98.93, 3.05, 9.62, 8.30, 9.07, 6.90, 5.83, 7.81, 7.81, 7.75, 7.91 — the 98.93->3.05 step is a container death (FinishedAt 2026-08-07T05:57:26.041Z, StartedAt 05:57:26.416Z, RestartCount 0->1, OOMKilled=false ExitCode=0), and the script scored it as a reclamation dip and emitted FOLD.

ROOT CAUSE (source-read, two independent defects that compound):
(1) STATE IS READ ONCE, BEFORE THE SAMPLE LOOP, AND NEVER RE-READ. Lines 50-51 capture RESTARTS=$(docker inspect .RestartCount) and STARTED=$(docker inspect .State.StartedAt); the sample loop is line 62; nothing re-reads them afterwards. The emitted JSON state block therefore reported restart_count=0 / started_at=2026-08-06T23:21:41Z for a run whose own samples span the restart. A death inside the window is structurally invisible to the script.
(2) THE DIP TEST TREATS A CRASH CLIFF AS RECLAMATION. Line 83: if(prev>=0 && (prev-v)>0.5){dips++}. ANY drop over 0.5pp counts as a reclamation dip, so a 95.88pp crash cliff is counted as the single strongest possible evidence of healthy reclamation. It simultaneously drags min_pct to 3.05, which independently defeats the ">97pct sustained" tripwire, while dips>0 defeats the "all samples >93pct with NO dip" tripwire (line 95). Both tripwires are therefore defeated BY THE VERY EVENT THEY EXIST TO CATCH — a container death during the window is GUARANTEED to yield FOLD, never ESCALATE.

IMPACT: this is the discriminator the auditor and PO/router triage chains use to decide whether an A-30 memory finding is real. It converts the most severe possible outcome into an all-clear. On this tick the auditor Tier-1 c77 escalation (sys-20260807T054825-771b) was CORRECT and the discriminator contradicted it 9 minutes before the container died.

FIX (deterministic, small): (a) re-read RestartCount and StartedAt AFTER the sample loop; if either changed, force VERDICT=ESCALATE with reason "container died/restarted during window" and surface both the before and after values in the state block; (b) exclude post-restart samples from min/max/dip analysis, or segment the window at the restart boundary; (c) add a guard so a single-step drop greater than some large threshold (e.g. >40pp) is classified as a discontinuity, never a dip, even if state re-read is somehow unavailable. Add a regression test replaying this exact 12-sample series and asserting ESCALATE.

RELATED: memory lesson feedback_a30_discriminator_crash_cliff_misscored_as_reclamation_dip records this same shape observed 2026-08-05 by router. It was NOT fixed then — this is a live re-fire on a real death, so it is a recurring-failed-fix, not a first observation.
done_tasks.verification_gate: regression test replays the 2026-08-07T05:56Z 12-sample series (99.01,98.93,3.05,...) plus a RestartCount delta and asserts verdict==ESCALATE
done_tasks.po_amendment_20260807T0610Z:
SHARPENED AFTER READING THE FULL VERDICT CHAIN (po, same tick). The defect is stronger and simpler than "a crash cliff is miscounted as a dip". The actual verdict logic is:

  VERDICT=FOLD (default)
  if   OOMKilled==true                      -> ESCALATE
  elif DIPS==0 && min_pct>93                -> ESCALATE
  elif DIPS==0 && max_pct>97                -> ESCALATE

BOTH percentage-based escalation branches are hard-gated on DIPS -eq 0. A "dip" is any sample-to-sample drop over 0.5pp (line 83). Therefore ONE single 0.5pp GC wobble anywhere in a 12-sample window forces FOLD unconditionally, no matter how severe every other sample is. Sustained 99pct with one 0.6pp jitter = FOLD. That is not a threshold, it is an all-or-nothing veto on the entire percentage plane.

The ONLY escalation path that survives a dip is OOMKilled==true. But this fleets documented memory-death signature is OOMKilled=false / ExitCode=0 — the Docker-Desktop VM-plane reap plus Bun mmap page-fault mode, already root-caused on FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP and restated on FIX-MCP-MEMORY-CODE-LEAKs own po_emergency_deploy_auth_20260805T1940Z field ("ExitCode=0+OOMKilled=false IS the fleets already-root-caused memory-death signature"). The 2026-08-07T05:57:26Z death confirms it again: OOMKilled=false, ExitCode=0.

NET: on this fleet the script CANNOT emit ESCALATE for a real memory death under any circumstances. The dip-gated branches are defeated by the death itself (the crash cliff is the largest possible "dip"), and the dip-immune branch is keyed on a flag this fleets memory deaths never set. Every escalation path is closed. That is why 2026-08-07T05:56:47-06:01:44Z returned FOLD across an actual container death.

THIRD DEFECT, SAME FILE — the VmHWM narrative veto. Line ~54 comment and the emitted vm.note both assert "VmHWM (peak RSS) vs VmRSS (current). HWM >> RSS proves reclamation already occurred." VmHWM is the monotonic non-decreasing high-water mark of VmRSS, so VmHWM >= VmRSS is TRUE BY DEFINITION at all times, including during terminal saturation. It proves nothing. It is not consumed by the verdict if-chain, so it is not a code-level veto — it is a NARRATIVE veto in the output that the human/agent reading the JSON uses to ratify FOLD. Live proof it misleads: during the 2026-08-07T05:54Z window VmHWM was ADVANCING (3170004 -> 3183020 kB), i.e. the process was setting new peaks minutes before dying, and the note still read as proof of healthy reclamation. THIS IS THE DEFECT THE MISSING ROW FIX-AUDITOR-A30-VMHWM-VETO-TAUTOLOGY-FALSE-NEGATIVE WAS NAMED FOR — that id is referenced as a depends[] by FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-A30-MEM-SINGLE-CONTAINER-SCOPE (review[]) but exists in NO lane and NO archive: a dangling dependency that would block that row forever. Folded here rather than minting the phantom id, and that rows depends[] has been repointed at THIS row this tick.

REVISED FIX SET: (a) re-read RestartCount/StartedAt after the loop; any delta -> ESCALATE "container died during window", surface before/after in state; (b) stop gating the percentage branches on DIPS==0 — evaluate sustained-high independently of jitter (e.g. escalate when the Nth percentile or the window median exceeds the threshold), since a 0.5pp wobble is not evidence of health; (c) classify any single-step drop >40pp as a discontinuity, never a dip; (d) add ExitCode==0 && FinishedAt-delta as an accepted death signature alongside OOMKilled, because this fleet never sets OOMKilled on memory death; (e) delete or rewrite the VmHWM claim — compare VmHWM against the cgroup limit and against its own previous value across the window (advancing HWM at the cap = escalate), never against VmRSS. Regression test replays the 2026-08-07T05:56Z 12-sample series plus the RestartCount 0->1 delta and asserts ESCALATE.
absorbs: FIX-AUDITOR-A30-VMHWM-VETO-TAUTOLOGY-FALSE-NEGATIVE (phantom id — referenced as depends[] by FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-A30-MEM-SINGLE-CONTAINER-SCOPE but never existed in any lane or archive)

This row has the inverse property, and that distinction is the entire basis for treating the two differently — verify-a30-mcp-memory-reclamation.sh returns FOLD across a window containing a REAL container death (reproduced live 2026-08-07T05:56:47-06:01:44Z, FinishedAt 05:57:26.041Z, RestartCount 0 to 1), and it is the discriminator the auditor/PO/router triage chain uses to decide whether an A-30 finding is real. That is a live, present-tense false-negative on the most severe outcome the detector exists to catch, and it is a recurring-failed-fix (same shape recorded 2026-08-05 in feedback_a30_discriminator_crash_cliff_misscored_as_reclamation_dip, not fixed then). done_tasks.title: Tier-1 A-30 memory check inspects 1 of 13 containers — hardcoded 'mcp-server' scope makes 11 capped containers permanently invisible to the only memory detector in Tier-1 (rag-service sat at 98.46% of cap while the same tick reported HEALTHY / 0 anomalies)
done_tasks.root_cause: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh:209 _check_mem_creep() hardcodes its subject: ctr=$(docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -i 'mcp-server' | head -1). Line 211's failure string ('mcp-server container not found via docker ps') confirms the scope is deliberate-but-narrow, not an accident of parsing. The tuned WARN_PCT=85 predicate at :224 is then applied to that ONE container and nothing else. Tier-1 has no other memory check, at any threshold, for any other container — so 12 of the 13 running containers have ZERO memory coverage in the tier whose job is first-line health. DEMONSTRATED FALSE-PASS (router-verified, same tick): 2026-07-25 08:30Z Tier-1 reported 'A-30 Memory: 58.63% — PASS' + HEALTHY / 0 anomalies (commit 4280e27f5) while docker stats showed rag-service 727.8MiB/768MiB = 94.76%, rising to 756.1MiB = 98.46% by 08:45Z. Router 10-probe / 4-min window (08:48:04Z-08:52:01Z, 25s spacing): pinned 756.1-756.2MiB / 98.46%, ZERO reclamation dips; per-process VmHWM 775224kB > VmRSS 762236kB (reclamation HAD occurred earlier, so the flat line is a real plateau not a measurement artifact). Service was serving correctly throughout (docker health=healthy, FailingStreak=0, /health 200, /search 200, /index 200). PO re-verified at 08:56Z: rag-service 756.2MiB/768MiB 98.46%, mcp-server 1.708GiB/3GiB 56.94%, every other container <= 16.88%. NOT a threshold-tuning problem and NOT agent error — the check cannot look at the container, so no threshold value could ever have caught it. Script is clean in git (no uncommitted edits) and git log on it shows the last 3 commits touched launchd checks only (b9484fa7a, e0d9187cd, 84096f617) — the scope line is live and untouched.
done_tasks.deliverable: (a) SCOPE — replace the single grep'd container with a loop over EVERY running container that declares a memory cap. Resolve the set from the LIVE daemon, never a hardcoded name list and never docker-compose.yml (which is config-truth, not runtime-truth — the two already drift, see FU-RUNTIME-SET-TRUTH-RECONCILE). Discriminator VERIFIED live 2026-07-25T08:56Z: `docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} {{.HostConfig.Memory}}' $(docker ps -q)` returns a byte cap per container and exactly 0 for uncapped — today 12 capped + mcp-gateway at 0. SKIP the uncapped ones: docker stats reports their MemPerc against total host memory (mcp-gateway prints 0.27% of 7.753GiB), which is not a headroom signal and would be a meaningless comparand against WARN_PCT. (b) PREDICATE — apply the SAME already-tuned WARN_PCT=85 boundary per container. Do NOT introduce per-container threshold constants (see PO DECISION). (c) MESSAGE — the failure string must name the ACTUAL container(s) over the line; today :225 hardcodes the words 'mcp-server mem' so a widened loop would mislabel every other container's breach as mcp-server. Report all breaching containers in one detail line, not just the first. (d) Drop the `head -1` silent-multi-match on the resolution path — with a loop it is dead, and it was always a silent-truncation hazard. (e) LEDGER — extend the acknowledged-degraded suppression to memory (see PO DECISION), seeded with the rag-service entry.
done_tasks.note: PO DECISION — the router correctly flagged the design tension: rag-service's normal set-point IS legitimately high (98.46% flat, healthy, serving), so a flat 85% across all containers would manufacture a fresh every-tick false positive and re-open exactly the churn the DONE row FIX-AUDITOR-A12A20A30-FP-REEMIT-CONVERGE just closed. RESOLVE IT WITH THE ACK LEDGER, NOT WITH THRESHOLDS. The mechanism already EXISTS and is LIVE in this same script — FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-ACKED-LAUNCHD-DEATH-SUPPRESSION shipped it at commit b9484fa7a: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh:255-330 reads docs/data/auditor-launchd-ack.json, and a listed condition that already has an OPEN backlog fix-row is reported as 'acknowledged-degraded (suppressed)' instead of flipping the verdict, WITH two guarantees that are exactly what is needed here: (1) mixed case never suppresses — an unacknowledged breach alongside acked ones still FAILS, so no permanent blindness; (2) a documented STALENESS RULE — the entry is removed once its tracked_by row reaches DONE_VERIFIED, so suppression cannot outlive the fix. Extend that ledger with a parallel acked_memory[] array (or a sibling docs/data/auditor-mem-ack.json) keyed by container/service name + tracked_by + acked_at, honouring the identical two guarantees, and SEED IT with rag-service tracked_by RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND. That single seed row is what makes a flat-85 loop safe on day one. EXPLICITLY REJECTED: per-container hardcoded threshold overrides. They are a static list that lags reality — the identical failure mode is already an open bug on this same probe family (FIX-AUDITOR-D4-WHITELIST-DATA-QUALITY-ANOMALY-PREFIX: a whitelist authored 2026-07-08 never learned a lock kind introduced 2026-07-19). A per-container 99% override for rag would also silently swallow a REAL rag OOM approach, whereas an ack entry pointing at an open row is self-expiring and auditable. ALSO REJECTED: moving WARN_PCT globally — it is the value the converge row tuned. OUT OF SCOPE (do NOT fold in): an absolute-headroom secondary predicate. 11.9MiB free on a 768m cap is thin in absolute terms and a pure percentage genuinely is not comparable across a 512m and a 3g cap, but adding a second predicate in the same change would confound the FP evidence for the first; mint it separately later if the loop proves the percentage view insufficient. FOLDED IN, NOT RE-MINTED (router prior-art, PO re-confirmed against all 12 board lanes): mcp-server 45.20%->58.63%/90min on ~11h uptime is BELOW the trajectory documented in FIX-MCP-MEMORY-CODE-LEAK ('87% in 12h from a 5% start') — benign, already tracked, no corroboration entry needed. rag-service RestartCount=12 today matches the ~10/day rate already documented in FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP — folded, not novel. Any proposal to RAISE rag-service's 768m limit belongs as a corroboration entry on FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY (and is user-gated infra anyway), never on this row. The mechanism behind rag's high set-point is already tracked at RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND (REVIEW, P1: _build_fts_index OOM-crashes the 768m container at ~56k rows) — this row does NOT fix rag's memory, it fixes the detector's blindness to it. PO independent prior-art scan 2026-07-25T08:56Z: full-text jq over all 12 task_board lanes (backlog 389 / review 105 / ready 45 / done 16 / in_progress 1 / active_sprints 8 / closed_sprints 19 / archive 7) for MemPerc|docker stats|per-container|multi-container|all-container returned 4 rows, all inspected: FIX-MCP-MEMORY-CODE-LEAK, FIX-AUDITOR-A12A20A30-FP-REEMIT-CONVERGE (DONE — shipped threshold/sampling/dedup tune, did NOT touch scope; :209 still hardcodes one container), RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND, FIX-MCP-DOCKERFILE-ENTRYPOINT-KNOWNHOSTS-REGRESSION. NONE covers multi-container memory detector coverage. Router's fold list confirmed correct; mint stands.

done_tasks.root_cause: PO OBSERVED BEFORE-AND-AFTER STATES, NOT THE WRITE ITSELF — the inference boundary is stated explicitly below. MEASURED: at 2026-07-29T10:41Z the working-tree docs/data/orch/orch-state.json contained 133 .signal_queue.rows[], including sys-20260729T103337-13e5 and sys-20260729T103338-7f95 (both type=data_stale, severity=WARN, to=po, status=NEW, summary 'sbv_fx stale 32min (check B-12)'). PO read them twice in separate jq invocations, so this is not a torn mid-write read. At 2026-07-29T10:52Z both were absent, .signal_queue.rows[] was 132, and both were absent from .signal_queue.archive[] as well — so they were not triaged, not archived, not cold-evicted-with-retention. They are absent from commit 3e257beba (authored 12:47:15 +0200 = 10:47:15Z, 'drain 2026-07-29T10:37Z tick'), whose committed file carries 131 rows — byte-identical signal_queue.rows[] id-set to its own parent 3e257beba~1 (comm -13/-23 both empty, i.e. that commit added and removed NOTHING from signal_queue). 131 committed + the 2 uncommitted rows = the 133 PO read. So a peer serialized a 131-row full-document baseline over a 133-row working tree and committed it, silently discarding two rows that had never been committed. THE WRITE GATE CANNOT CATCH THIS AND IS NOT SUPPOSED TO: scripts/orch-apply.sh delegates to scripts/orch-conservation-check.mjs, whose FLOOR_RATIO defaults to 0.5 (line 64) and which only flags when a candidate total drops BELOW HALF of live (line 158). 131/133 = 98.5%, so a 2-row loss passes trivially. That design decision is defensible for bulk eviction and is NOT the thing to revert — but it means NOTHING in the system currently protects an individual untriaged signal_queue row from being dropped by a stale-baseline write.
