The guard is doing its documented job; the gap is that NO guard owns single-row loss. (2) DO NOT fix this by telling agents to re-read before writing. Every agent already believes it does; the losing write here came from a flow that produced a full-document baseline, and prose cannot make a stale in-memory snapshot fresh. The CAS/rename path in orch-apply.sh is the place where a stale baseline is mechanically detectable. (3) DO NOT assume the CAS guard already covers it — it demonstrably did not on this occurrence; establish WHY before designing (candidate built from a pre-read snapshot, a bypass env var, or a write that never went through orch-apply.sh at all are all live hypotheses and they have different fixes). (4) DO NOT scope this to the signal drain flow alone until the actor is identified. PO did not observe the write and names no culprit flow; 3e257beba is the commit that PUBLISHED the 131-row state, which is not the same claim as it having authored the loss.

done_tasks.root_cause: MECHANISM (PO-verified by execution 2026-07-29T10:20-10:28Z; supersedes DIAGNOSE-RAG-SERVICE-RESTART-LOOP). TWO STACKED CAUSES. (1) FIXED BASELINE EATS THE CAP: embedder.py _model is a lazy singleton (:37 init None, :51 _ensure_model_loaded) with NO release path — grep of apps/rag-service/**/*.py for unload|.release(|del self._model|gc.collect|empty_cache returns ONLY the :37 initializer, so once loaded the model is resident for the container's life. MEASURED on the live container: cold RSS 50.7 MiB (6.6% of 768 MiB); model load logged 10:24:28.5Z->10:24:48.9Z on the FIRST embed; docker stats immediately after, having served exactly ONE POST /index: 749.9 MiB / 768 MiB = 97.65%. HEADROOM 18.1 MiB. (The embedder docstring's '~600-700 MiB warm' understates live by ~50-150 MiB.) Cap was halved in 2dc1d8c4e (Wed Jun 10 2026, 'reduce memory limits to 512m/768m', diff -memory:1.5g/+memory:768m; rag block docker-compose.yml L165-171) for host-budget reasons and never re-validated against the model's fixed cost. (2) COMPACTION FAILURE-PATH DOES NOT RESET ITS COUNTER — this is a real code defect, NOT tuning. repositories.py compact() :237-259 puts 'self._insert_count = 0' at :251 INSIDE the try, AFTER 'await table.optimize(cleanup_older_than=...)' at :250; the except at :257-259 logs a WARNING and returns NORMALLY without resetting. insert() :230-235 wraps 'await self.compact()' in its own try/except whose handler DOES reset (:235 'self._insert_count = 0  # reset to avoid tight retry loop') — but that handler is UNREACHABLE because compact() already swallowed the exception. NET: on ANY compaction failure the counter stays >= _COMPACT_EVERY, so EVERY SUBSEQUENT INSERT re-fires a full-table optimize() until one attempt happens to win. The code's own comment names the exact failure it fails to prevent. LIVE PROOF of the burst: 2026-07-29T09:02:36.139Z / 09:02:36.140Z / 09:02:40.06Z / 09:02:43.13Z all 'compaction failed (non-fatal)' -> 09:02:44.17Z 'compaction complete' -> 09:02:44.75Z failed again = SIX full-table optimize() calls in 8.6 s. Failure modes seen: 'Retryable commit conflict for version 12326/12331: This Rewrite transaction was preempted by concurrent transaction Rewrite' and 'Object at location .../_versions/18446744073709542049.manifest not found'. The retry the engine explicitly asks for is never performed. CADENCE PROOF: 6h window = 770 POST /index vs 14 compaction attempts (8 complete + 6 failed) = 55 inserts/attempt against a nominal _COMPACT_EVERY=100 — it is over-firing by ~1.8x. CAUSAL JOIN: each optimize() is a FULL-TABLE rewrite emitting a ~20 MiB fragment (5 largest data files all 19.4-20.0 MiB); firing bursts of those inside 18.1 MiB of headroom is the death event. Because the allocation is in the Rust lance extension and PID 1 unwinds, the container dies as ExitCode=0 / OOMKilled=false — so ANY triage keying on OOMKilled misses this class entirely. CORROBORATION (unplanned, disclosed by the spike): a 'docker exec python3 -c import lancedb' shares the cgroup and killed the container at 10:12:00.6Z; anon fell 726.4 -> 30.8 MiB across the restart, proving the memory is process-resident, not reclaimable page cache. done_tasks.status_note:
THREE COUPLED DEFECTS, all PO-verified at source 2026-07-25T14:50Z. Fix all three or the loop returns.

(A) POISON VALUE DEFEATS THE SORT — scripts/orch-cold-evict.sh:236. `sort_by(.created_at // "0000-00-00T00:00:00Z")` is a plain STRING sort, and the `//` alternative only substitutes when created_at is null/absent. It does NOT catch the literal string "unknown". 10 of the 16 live done[] rows carry created_at:"unknown" (ARCH-ORCH-F1, ARCH-ORCH-F2, ARCH-ORCH-QA, BCTC-CURRENT-404-INVESTIGATE, FDA-4, FDA-8, FU-LOCKSTORE-EXPIRED-GC, FU-PRESSURE-EMIT-DARK, FU-TICK-SNAPSHOT-EMIT-DARK, PM-ORCH-DASH-DECISION-DRILLDOWN). 'u' (0x75) > '2' (0x32), so after sort_by|reverse those 10 rank as the NEWEST rows, keys 0-9. They therefore consume the ENTIRE KEEP_RECENT_DONE=10 window and fail `.key >= keep_n` forever — even though they would PASS the age gate, because line 245's `try (created_at|fromdateiso8601) catch 0` maps them to epoch 0. The malformed value makes the oldest rows look newest. Schema permits it: orchStateSchema.ts:102 `created_at: z.string().optional()` — any string, no ISO-8601 refinement. No live writer of "unknown" found in scripts/ (grep clean), so this is legacy data, not an active producer.

(B) TRIGGER AND ACTION ARE ON DIFFERENT AXES — scripts/agents-flow/dev-team-tick-preflight.sh:368 fires Step 5.5 when ANY of {terminal_sprint_n>0, sprint_goal_terminal_n>0, done_n>10, dv_n>0}. Live right now: 0 / 0 / 16 / 0 — so `done_n > 10` is the SOLE live disjunct. The action it fires (orch-cold-evict.sh:242-247) evicts a done row only when `.key >= keep_n` AND created_at older than `now - DONE_MAX_AGE_DAYS*86400` (default 7d, line 66). A COUNT gate firing a COUNT-AND-AGE action cannot be self-clearing. Even with (A) fixed the loop RETURNS: the 6 well-formed done rows accumulated over 4 days (~1.5/day), so a 7-day age window holds ~10 rows on its own and done_n re-crosses 10 within roughly a week. (A) alone buys about seven days, not a fix.

(C) THE ACCEPTANCE INSTRUMENT ITSELF LIES — orch-cold-evict.sh:256 `[.task_board.done_verified // [] | .[].id // ""]`. jq's `//` fires when the LHS produces NO outputs, so on an EMPTY array this yields `[""]`, length 1. Live proof: done_verified is `[]` and signal_queue.archive is `[]`, yet --dry-run prints 'done_verified[] would evict: 1 items' and 'signal_queue.archive[] evict: 1 items'. Harmless for actual eviction (the `select(. != "")` at 258-260 drops the phantom) but it corrupts the exact report an operator or a test would read to decide whether a run did anything. Confirm with: jq -n '[[] | .[].id // ""]' -> [""]. Same shape guards n_evict_done at line 344. FIX (C) FIRST — the acceptance test for (A)/(B) reads this report.

So Arm B is not merely a fallback for cycles that die silently — it is a **cross-plane invariant** that holds even when every agent-side check passes. Reframe it that way in the deliverable: the pre-gate-vs-return diff must fire on ANY upstream-FAILURE/downstream-GREEN pair regardless of which plane is at fault, precisely because the faulty plane is the one that cannot report itself.

Getting this wrong would make Arm B fire on every acked-suppression tick and get itself switched off.

done_tasks.root_cause: apps/stock-price/pkg/infrastructure/fetchers.go:303 (SQLitePriceHistoryRepository.GetHistory) and :240 (Tier3Fetcher) build the DSN 'file:%s?mode=ro&_journal_mode=WAL&_busy_timeout=5000'. The live market.db has PRAGMA journal_mode=delete, so the driver issuing PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL over a mode=ro connection fails with SQLITE_READONLY(8) 'attempt to write a readonly database'. The resulting db.Query error is then discarded at fetchers.go:318-320 ('return []domain.DailyOHLCV{}, nil //nolint:nilerr'), with the same swallow at :305-307 for sql.Open — so the handler emits HTTP 200 with an empty history and logs nothing. The two SIBLING repositories in this same package already fixed exactly this: foreign_flow_repository.go:33 and room_event_repository.go:32 both carry the comment 'Note: readonly mode (mode=ro) conflicts with WAL journal mode creation.' and dropped mode=ro from their DSN. The correction was applied to 2 of 4 call sites; fetchers.go:240 and :303 were missed.

done_tasks.product_question_decide_before_scoping: ANSWER THIS FIRST — the fix does not follow from the defect. Question as router framed it: if a news-inference fallback only ever produces directional hints and never real balance-sheet figures, is writing it into financial_reports — the table bctcIdentityGuard treats as authoritative at serve time — the actual design error, such that guarding arm (b2) alone merely relocates the problem? PO'S STRONG STEER, WITH THE PROOF: YES, IT IS THE DESIGN ERROR, and here is the reductio that settles it. Arm (b1) already blocks every write where a good row exists. Arm (b2), applied literally, blocks every write where NO row exists AND totalAssets<=0. Since totalAssets is hardcoded 0 on EVERY call (verified above — no path produces otherwise), the two arms together block 100% of this function's writes. Adding arm (b2) does not fix the function; it silently converts it into a total no-op while leaving ~600 lines of live, tested, maintained code in place pretending to be a working fallback. A guard that makes its own subject unreachable is not a guard — it is proof that the write target is wrong. CORROBORATING, AND THE PART THAT MAKES THIS USER-FACING RATHER THAN MERELY UNTIDY: (i) the code's OWN comment at lines 254-259 already concedes the whole argument — 'this fallback ALWAYS writes totalAssets=0 ... it reconstructs directional hints from news signals, never real balance-sheet figures — i.e. every call is, by construction, the exact OCR-corruption fingerprint bctcIdentityGuard.ts checks for at serve time.' The codebase has already diagnosed itself; nobody drew the conclusion. (ii) The write is strictly WORSE than not writing, because it destroys an honest signal: an absent row serves 'Chua co du lieu BCTC' ('we do not have this'), whereas a zeros row serves '[CORRUPT DATA - SKIP] total_assets=0 (OCR extraction failure)' — a false claim that we HAVE the filing and it is broken, which misattributes a defect to the filer. This is the same family of harm as the ngay_nop flip on the parent row: fabricating a state that defames a real-world filing. (iii) buildAnalysisSummary() at line 73 formats this into Vietnamese RAG-retrievable prose — 'Tong tai san: 0 trieu dong.' — a flat factual assertion that the company has zero total assets, written into the retrieval corpus. That is fabricated financial data in a served surface, and it engages feedback_no_fake_data_real_fetch directly. THEREFORE the design target to evaluate is: directional news-inference hints belong in a hints/signals surface, NOT in financial_reports. BA must still evaluate the alternatives honestly (a separate table/column; a nullable-financials sentinel row explicitly marked non-authoritative that bctcIdentityGuard excludes; or deleting the write path entirely and keeping the function as a pure read-side hint producer) — my steer is not a pre-selected implementation, and if BA finds a consumer that genuinely needs these rows in financial_reports, say so and I will revisit.

(2) plan_only FIRST MOVE EXECUTED AND DISCHARGED. The row specified: "correlate /health sessionCount against MemPerc over several hours on the POST-deploy image before any code change". Done, on a 6h31m-old cold-started container: /health sessions = 871 -> 873 across an 84s window (~+86/h). "Sequential Market Analysis tool registered" = 4018 occurrences since boot = 4018 McpServer constructions in 6h31m, of which 873 were still resident -> roughly 78pct of sessions DO get reaped by res.on(close), the residual ~22pct never do. MemPerc 98.19-99.01pct across 22 probes in 2 independent windows. 2.974GiB / 873 sessions ~= 3.5MB per leaked session, consistent with an McpServer holding 183 registered tools. VmHWM ADVANCED 3170004 -> 3183020 kB DURING the observation window: high-water still climbing at the cap, not a stable sawtooth.

(3) TERMINAL EVENT — the correlation ended in a real death, observed live. Container FinishedAt 2026-08-07T05:57:26.041Z, StartedAt 05:57:26.416Z (375ms Docker auto-restart), RestartCount 0->1, OOMKilled=false ExitCode=0 = the fleets already-root-caused memory-death signature (identical to FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP), NOT a clean exit. Post-restart sessions=14, MemPerc 3.05->7.91pct. Time from cold start to death: 6h36m. This is the answer to "does the leak fix hold": the 609f62800 fix holds for what it targeted, and this second leak alone is sufficient to kill the container in under 7 hours.

(4) MECHANISM, source-read at apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/transport.ts — CONFIRMS the architect Finding 2 and adds WHY the existing cleanup cannot save it. handleSse() line 95 does `const mcpServer = this.createServer()`; that McpServer is a bare local, never stored on the instance and never .close()d. res.on("close") (lines 84-92) deletes ONLY the transport Map entry and the heartbeat interval. The only other eviction path is the heartbeat catch block (lines 69-78), which fires only if `res.write()` THROWS SYNCHRONOUSLY. Nodes res.write() on a broken pipe does not throw — it buffers and emits "error" on the socket. So for any client that vanishes without a clean FIN (the normal case for a killed/timed-out cowork agent or a dropped Cloudflare tunnel), NEITHER eviction path can fire and the Map entry is permanent. The documented "cleanup gated solely on res.on(close) or write-failure" is therefore, in practice, gated on res.on(close) ALONE — the write-failure branch is effectively dead code. No idle reaper, no max-age, no DELETE handler.

(5) DESIGN CONSTRAINT for architect: a reaper keyed on transport liveness alone is insufficient — it must also close the per-session McpServer (mcpServer.close()), otherwise the SDK-side registration graph for 183 tools stays reachable. Recommend: retain the McpServer alongside the transport in a single per-session record, add an idle/max-age reaper (last-activity timestamp bumped in handleMessage), and add a DELETE /sse handler. Correlate sessionCount against MemPerc post-fix to confirm.

(6) FILES[] PATH CORRECTED: this rows files[0] read apps/mcp-server/src/interface/transport.ts, which DOES NOT EXIST. Real path is apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/transport.ts. Corrected in place so architect/dev are not sent to a non-existent file.

=== PO SIGN-OFF 2026-08-14T04:11:35Z (REVIEW-lane, claimed by dev-team secondary-drain 2026-08-14T04:03:05Z, commit 1c81fab4a) ===

VERDICT: APPROVED. The 403-line design doc answers all five questions the SPIKE asked, is grounded in 20 code-verified brownfield paths rather than assertion, and its single most valuable finding is a NEGATIVE one: it proves the current escalation path is a dead end BY DESIGN (alert-commander correctly suppresses infra noise — wrong addressee, not a bug), which is what makes the redirect the crux rather than a nice-to-have. Timebox 120min honoured. Reuse discipline held: 2 new pure-domain files, 2 infra files, 1 signal writer, 1 additive table — everything else extends live mechanisms.

ANSWERS TO §10 OPEN QUESTIONS:

Q1 — bucket 3 (~14 MCP-REST computed gauges: indicator-gauges x5, momentum-indicators x5, money-radar x4): ACCEPT the architect's 'upstream-bounded, no independent probe' disposition. NO 4th bucket-3 follow-up will be sized. Rationale: these gauges are DERIVED from daily_ohlcv/market_prices/news_articles, which the legacy price/technical/news signal types already cover — 14 redundant per-gauge probes is precisely the per-source point-patch multiplication this SPIKE was opened to end, and it would put 14 new CRITICAL emitters in front of an anti-spam layer that has not yet proven itself in production. ONE PRODUCT REQUIREMENT ATTACHED so the frontend does not silently lose accuracy: each bucket-3 row in docs/data/frontend-data-coverage-map.json must carry an additive `upstream_bounded_by: <table>` annotation, so FIX-L3-FRONTEND-AUTOREFRESH-FRESHNESS-BADGE can render the UPSTREAM's freshness on the gauge badge instead of rendering nothing. That is a JSON annotation, not a probe — it belongs in the bucket-2 widening row, not its own task. Revisit only if a live user-visible incident is ever traced to a gauge that was stale while its upstream was fresh.

Q2 — new `surface_breach_audit` table vs relaxing `sla_breach_audit`'s CHECK constraint: APPROVED, build the NEW additive table exactly as designed. Two independent reasons. (i) Risk asymmetry: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is zero-risk on a live DB; relaxing a CHECK on a table that 12 legacy signal types already write requires a rebuild-and-copy on SQLite (no ALTER ... DROP CONSTRAINT), i.e. a genuine migration on shared production data, to buy nothing. (ii) The two things being stored are not the same KIND of key: `sla_breach_audit.signal_type` is a CLOSED 12-value allowlist, coverage-map surfaces are an OPEN namespace that grows whenever a row is added to frontend-data-coverage-map.json. Merging an open namespace into a closed allowlist is a failure mode this repo has already paid for once (signal-row type open-namespace vs closed-allowlist, 4x redispatch, root-caused 2026-08-13). Keep the closed allowlist closed; give the open namespace its own table. HARD CONSTRAINT ON THE IMPLEMENTER: do not touch `sla_breach_audit`'s DDL or its CHECK list in the same change.

Q3 — isVnMarketHours 02:00->02:15 as its own fast FIX: AGREED, and it is ALREADY MINTED — FIX-SLA-MONITOR-MARKET-OPEN-BOUNDARY-DETERMINISTIC-DAILY-BREACH (backlog, dev-mcp-server, created 2026-08-07T02:50:38Z, i.e. before the brief was written). NOT re-minted; reprioritized P2 -> P1 and the brief's line-level root cause (freshnessSlaChecker.ts:144-159) cross-linked onto it. See that row's own PO note for how the boundary shift and its AC-1 warm-up compose rather than compete.

TWO CONSTRAINTS PO ADDS ON TOP OF THE DESIGN (both carried onto every minted row):
1. FAIL-OPEN IS NON-NEGOTIABLE (the design's own §9 bullet, promoted here to an acceptance criterion): an unresolvable or errored probe returns NO VERDICT and falls back to the legacy age-only check — never a fabricated CRASH. A classifier that manufactures false CRASH FIX rows is strictly worse than today's silence, because today's failure mode costs nothing and that one costs PO triage capacity on every tick.
2. NO ROW MAY BE CLOSED ON A GREEN UNIT TEST ALONE. The design's own live-acceptance criterion is the closing gate: at a real 02:00Z tick, `bash scripts/check-foreign-flow-freshness.sh` reports verdict=PASS while the classifier emits NO CRITICAL for foreign_flow or price. Both PO-folded false positives (foreign_flow 3899/1020/1020min; price 44/59/59min, all at 02:00Z = 09:00 ICT, before the 09:15 open) must be regression fixtures in freshnessCadenceConfig's unit tests AND must be confirmed silent live.

SCOPE FENCE: FIX-L4-FRESHNESS-SLA-MONITOR-SELF-POLICING (detector) and FIX-L3-FRONTEND-AUTOREFRESH-FRESHNESS-BADGE (consumer) stay untouched by this decomposition, as the brief states. §9's flagged pre-existing duplication (vpsHealthPoller.ts's second, independent idle-vs-unhealthy classifier) is ACKNOWLEDGED AND DEFERRED — not folded in, not minted. Consolidating two live classifiers while replacing the escalation path of one of them is how a 4-row change becomes an incident; revisit after the TRIAGE layer is live and quiet for a week.

done_tasks.desc:
pdfOcrWorker.ts:extractAndStorePdfPages hard-caps OCR at 80 pages (line ~261, maxPages = Math.min(totalPages, 80)) but the completeness re-extraction gate (line ~217-219, threshold = Math.max(expectedPages * 0.5, 3)) checks the CAPPED extracted-page count against the UNCAPPED expected page count. For any PDF with totalPages > 160, 80 < threshold forever — the extraction is judged perpetually incomplete, DELETED (db.run "DELETE FROM pdf_extracted_text WHERE filename = ?") and re-OCR'd from scratch, capped at 80 again, on EVERY call — i.e. every single composition-root bootstrap OCR loop run (composition-root.ts §4b), forever, with zero possibility of ever satisfying the threshold.
LIVE CONFIRMED on vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1, 2 consecutive boots (2026-07-30T22:07:03Z, 2026-07-31T00:56:46Z), identical shape both times: GVR_2026_Q1.pdf (totalPages=204, extracted pinned at 80, threshold=102), GVR_2025_Q4.pdf (totalPages=285, extracted pinned at 80, threshold=142.5), 000000013535084_20240328__MSN__Bao_cao_thuong_nien_2023compressedsigned.pdf (totalPages=255, extracted pinned at 80, threshold=127.5) — DB query (bun:sqlite against /app/data/market.db) confirms all 3 sit at exactly c=80 rows, never advancing across boots. WHY IT IS DEAD, read at source (not inferred). The table's only writer is insertSignalQualityAudit() (infrastructure/db/signalQualityAuditStore.ts), reached from exactly one call site: post_agent_signal's handler at interface/mcp/tools/news-analysis/agentSignalTools.ts:455-500. Three preconditions must ALL hold: (1) the signal was not dedup-suppressed — note the `if (id <= 0) { ... return }` early-return sits ABOVE the audit block, so every dedup-suppressed post skips the audit silently; (2) signal_type is price_confirmation or urgent_news; (3) typeof finding_data.confidence === 'number'.

The suspected structural break is (3) against the emitter contract. domain/signals/signalTypes.ts makes confidence REQUIRED for price_confirmation (:159 z.number().min(0).max(1)) but OPTIONAL for urgent_news (:217 .optional()), and docs/agents/tools/package/news-scout.md:66 documents urgent_news's required finding_data as headline/source/severity — confidence is NOT in the documented required set. So a fully-compliant news-scout urgent_news post never trips the audit write. docs/agents/tools/list/get_signal_effectiveness.md shows urgent_news at 58 recorded signals; the audit table has 6 rows LIFETIME. price_confirmation, the one type that does mandate confidence, does not appear in that effectiveness sample at all.

BOTH failure modes are silent by construction: agentSignalTools.ts:499 catches and console.warn's ('non-fatal'), and signalQualityAuditStore.ts:78 catches and console.warn's again. Two swallow layers, no counter, no alarm. The SLA monitor is the only thing that ever noticed.

done_tasks.title: Foreign-flow pipeline outage renders NO bulletin section at all — the canonical "Du lieu khong kha dung (pipeline tam dung)" copy sits behind a branch the production SQL can never reach
done_tasks.root_cause: Verified at CODE level, not from comments. assembleEveningSummary.ts:571-580 selects foreign flow with `WHERE date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM daily_ohlcv) AND foreign_net_vol IS NOT NULL AND foreign_net_vol <> 0`. done_tasks.title: bctcReparseJob: double-wrap recordJobRun + ungated restart catch-up defeat the T4 cadence guard's evidentiary trail
done_tasks.detail: Found during SPIKE-BCTC-REPARSE-CADENCE-GUARD-ROOTCAUSE-VERIFY AC-2 (findings docs/spikes/SPIKE-BCTC-REPARSE-CADENCE-GUARD-ROOTCAUSE-VERIFY.md). runBctcReparseWithDb (apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/startupHelpers.ts:361-366) wraps recordJobRun(db,'bctcReparseJob',fn) where fn discards runBctcReparseJob()'s real ReparseRunResult (Promise<void> arrow fn) -- so cron_job_runs.rows_written is ALWAYS NULL for this job (RAW-confirmed live: 100% of ~90 sampled rows across 11 days, 2026-07-29). Worse: recordJobRun marks the row 'success' whenever fn() resolves without throwing, REGARDLESS of whether runBctcReparseJob()'s OWN shouldSkipRecoveryReplay guard (bctcReparseJob.ts:718) early-returned a no-op -- so a guard-SKIPPED invocation still writes a fresh 'success' row, silently re-arming its own 21.6h dedup window. This is the SAME double-wrap class already found+fixed for runBaseRateComputationWithDb (FIX-BASE-RATE-COMPUTATION-CRON-DEAD, 2026-07-23) and runEvidenceAccumulatorWithDb (EVIDENCE-ACCUM-SILENT-CRON) -- bctcReparseJob was never patched. It uniquely compounds with a SECOND defect: the startup catch-up in startScheduler.ts:169-182 fires runBctcReparseWithDb(db) UNCONDITIONALLY 30s after every container boot/restart with NO staleness gate -- its own introducing commit (75b729183, 2026-04-12) claimed to mirror runDailyAuditIfStale's pattern (dataAuditJob.ts:292-311, which correctly checks last_daily_audit_at age before running) but never implemented an equivalent check. Net effect, RAW-confirmed live (docker exec, market.db, last 30 days): 2-7 cron_job_runs rows per calendar day for bctcReparseJob (vs. the intended 1x/day), overwhelmingly 0-3ms duration (guard-skip echoes) with occasional real multi-hour runs, plus status='crashed' zombie rows on restart-cluster days (2026-07-19, 2026-07-28) -- the table's 'last success' signal is contaminated by boot-time noise unrelated to real reparse activity, and is the best-supported explanation for the 2026-07-10 incident this SPIKE investigated (ops' pre-edit probe showed clean, then a subsequent restart re-armed the guard within 30s, before ops resorted to falsifying 25 rows instead of using the job's own nowMsFn override).
done_tasks.ac: (1) runBctcReparseWithDb gains its own shouldSkipRecoveryReplay(db,'bctcReparseJob',DAILY_CADENCE_MS) check BEFORE calling recordJobRun (mirrors the FIX-BASE-RATE-COMPUTATION-CRON-DEAD fix pattern exactly) so a guard-skip never reaches recordJobRun and never writes a fresh row. (2) fn's default implementation captures runBctcReparseJob()'s real ReparseRunResult and maps resolved+failed to rowsWritten (or an equivalent field) so cron_job_runs.rows_written is no longer always NULL for this job. (3) startScheduler.ts's bctcReparseJob startup catch-up (currently unconditional, :169-182) gains a staleness gate consistent with its own stated intent to mirror runDailyAuditIfStale -- either reuse shouldRunCatchup() (matching the other 5 hardened catchups in the same file) or an equivalent last-run-age check, so a restart does not unconditionally fire the job every single boot. (4) new unit tests proving both fixes through the real default code paths (mirror FIX-BASE-RATE-COMPUTATION-CRON-DEAD.test.ts's approach) -- specifically a test that 2 back-to-back invocations within the cadence window produce exactly 1 cron_job_runs row, not 2. (5) RAW-verify post-fix: cron_job_runs rows-per-day for bctcReparseJob drops to <=1 on days without a genuine multi-file reparse, and rows_written is populated (non-NULL) on real runs.

done_tasks.title: windowPartitioner maxWindowPages truncation creates a headless tail window that continuation-stitch.md's contract never anticipated -- resolveColumnLayout() defaults to code-first, silently swapping code/label on label-first (bank) continuation tables split by the cap
done_tasks.root_cause: windowPartitioner.ts's maxWindowPages cap (windowPartitioner.ts:92-101) does NOT fold an over-cap continuation table into its current window -- it starts a brand-new window (i=j) at the very next page, which is itself a mid-table continuation page with no header of its own (that's why it matched CONTINUATION_MARKER in the first place). This 'tail window' gets page_type='continuation' (getBctcPendingRefineTool.ts:319-335) and is dispatched to the SAME sub-flow as a genuine first-page window (docs/agents/refine_bctc_md/flow/continuation-stitch.md), whose contract (Steps 2-3) unconditionally treats the window's first page as carrying the table's real header -- a rule that was never updated to anticipate a truncation-created headless tail. Downstream, refinedMarkdownParser.ts::resolveColumnLayout() (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:386-393) decides code-first vs label-first column order by reading the CAPTURED header row's own cell text, but headerCells is a per-call local re-initialized to null on every parseRefinedMarkdown invocation (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:439) -- unlike statement_section, which IS explicitly threaded window-to-window via initialSection/finalSection (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:404-419, finalizeBctcRefine.ts:162,174-175). A tail window with no header of its own (the expected shape) falls back to the DEFAULT code-first layout (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:387,391), silently swapping code<->label for every 4-column row of a label-first (bank Meu B02a/TCTDHN) continuation table whose true header only existed in the truncated head window. This corrupts (not drops) code/label text; value_current/value_prior are read from the same cell indices in both layouts so numeric values are unaffected. bctcScalarAggregator.ts resolves headline scalars (total_assets, equity_total, net_revenue, ...) via LABEL-CANONICAL matching preferred over code (bctcScalarAggregator.ts:20-21,396-399) and also uses row code/label shape for isBankFormFromRows bank-vs-corporate detection -- a swap can silently degrade or null the headline figures this pipeline exists to produce, with no error and no gate that catches it (checkSectionCompleteness/BEQ-7 only checks statement_section PRESENCE, never code/label correctness -- bctcSectionCompleteness.ts:27-60). Same root mechanism as the already-shipped FIX-BCTC-BANK-BS-COLUMN-ORDER (single-window, no-captured-header case) -- that fix added within-window header capture but never cross-window threading, so the maxWindowPages truncation path re-opens the identical hazard through a side door the original fix did not anticipate. Live-confirmed trigger frequency: 5 truncation WARNs within the same second of a single run (docs/agent-memory/health/team-tool-recheck-2026-06-21-1605.md:195-196) -- not a theoretical edge case. NOT independently reproduced within the spike's 120-min timebox: an actual corrupted bctc_table_rows row instance from a live truncation-tail window (would need pulling a real bctc_refined_units row past a report's first truncated unit_id and diffing against a known label-first bank filing).

po_amendment_6_20260814T1801Z.d_EC2_BOUNDEDNESS_ARGUMENT_REGROUNDED: The EC-2 conclusion (bounded-not-closed, defer to Phase 2) is CORRECT; its EVIDENCE BASE is not. SS3's comment grounds 'no live fire pattern can alias two different UTC windows onto the same (CYCLE_DATE, VN_HOUR) pair today' ENTIRELY in the declared cron string. Live artifacts refute the cron string as a bound on actual fire times: (1) docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-08-12-intraday.json carries cycle_id `intraday-2026-08-12T15:13Z` -- outside the declared 02-08 UTC window altogether (its own mtime 08:25Z indicates that stamp is a VN-local time mislabelled `Z`, which is a SECOND and fully independent reason SS4's cycle_id non-promotion rule is right, and worth adding to that comment); (2) run-start drift against the nominal window is real and measurable -- across 11 live intraday artifacts, cycle-start minus nominal fire runs +7 to +22 min (worst: 2026-08-07, nominal 04:13Z, cycle start 04:35Z). This matters because VN_HOUR is a run-start `date +%H` read (chef.md:105): the margin before the hour digit flips is 47 min (:13 to :00), and a live fire has already consumed ~47% of it. REQUIRED EDITS to the SS3 comment text before it is embedded: (i) re-ground the boundedness sentence on OBSERVED fire times plus the 47-minute run-start margin, not on the cron shape alone; (ii) widen the TRIPWIRE from 'any change to chef-intraday's cron in docs/data/cowork-schedule.json' to 'any change to the cron OR any observed fire outside the declared window' -- that schedule row now carries `_superseded_by: "cowork-dispatcher"` and `trigger_status: "deleted"`, so while the cron FIELD remains the live discriminator SSOT that chef.md:114 reads, it is no longer the ACTUATOR, and a cron-only tripwire can be bypassed by a dispatcher-side cadence change.
po_amendment_6_20260814T1801Z.e_FILENAME_VS_MUTEX_DATE_BASIS_DISAGREEM: The half of the parent row's binding 2026-07-22 CAUTION that this spec never confronts. SS4 quotes the CAUTION's cycle_id half accurately and discharges it. The CAUTION's other operative clause reads 'never a leaf-side `date`/run-start read ... so the filename key and the mutex key agree by construction' -- and VN_HOUR IS exactly a leaf-side run-start read. Verified at source, post-fix the two keys agree on the HOUR and DISAGREE on the DATE: filename = {CYCLE_DATE_UTC}-{SLOT_ID}-{VN_HOUR} (chef-dish.md:635 pins CYCLE_DATE = CYCLE_DATE_UTC) while the intraday mutex = published:{SLOT_ID}:{WORK_DATE}:{VN_HOUR} where WORK_DATE is the VN-local date (chef.md:104, 127). They coincide today ONLY because UTC 02-08 falls inside one VN calendar day -- i.e. CONTINGENTLY, not 'by construction' as stub TASK-003's own AC-2/NFR-3 framing claims. This does NOT block Phase 1: deferring to the window-anchor migration is the right call and the Phase-2 row exists. It must be RECORDED, in two places: (i) the SS3 EC-2 comment must state BOTH basis mixes -- VN_HOUR-vs-CYCLE_DATE_UTC inside the filename, AND CYCLE_DATE_UTC-vs-WORK_DATE between filename and mutex; (ii) the Phase-2 row FIX-CHEF-INTRADAY-MARKER-KEY-UTC-HOUR-BASIS-MIGRATION's AC-1 today names only the HOUR component ('both derive from the SAME scheduled_utc_time-derived UTC hour') -- it must be widened to migrate the DATE component in the same change, or Phase 2 will close half this defect and certify the whole of it closed.

Re-derived here: the real 2026-08-07 intraday artifact is docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-08-07-intraday.json with cycle start 04:35Z, i.e. VN hour 11 -- so its post-fix path is `-intraday-11.json`, NOT the `-intraday-09.json` the spec, the brief SS4.1, and stub TASK-003's AC-1/AC-2 all cite. The `-09` value is a sound arithmetic illustration of the 02:13Z window but it is not the day it names, and three documents now repeat it. FIX: relabel it as a SYNTHETIC example, or use the real 04:35Z/VN-11 pair. Same inherited-unverified-claim shape as part (b), on a numeric rather than an existence claim.
po_amendment_6_20260814T1801Z.g_NEW_AC5_SLOT_COMPONENT_NONDETERMINISM_: NEW ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, added rather than bounced -- the spec's own AC-1/AC-4 are not meaningful without it. The synthesis filename family carries TWO live slot-component conventions: 4 files use the `chef-`-prefixed slot_id (chef-eod x1, chef-evening x2, chef-intraday x1) against 64 using the bare dish_type. On 2026-08-13 BOTH shapes exist for the intraday slot ON THE SAME DAY -- unified-agent-synthesis-2026-08-13-chef-intraday.json (metadata: slot_id `chef-intraday`, cycle_utc 03:21Z, cycle_vn_hour 10, dish_type `convergence_scan`) alongside unified-agent-synthesis-2026-08-13-intraday.json (metadata: cycle_id `intraday-2026-08-13T08:13:00Z`, dish_type `intraday`) -- and the two carry DIFFERENT metadata schemas, which is the same schema-instability harm the parent's own po_measurement_20260730T2148 recorded for the bctc family, now demonstrated on the chef family. Three consequences, all acceptance-bearing: (1) SS8's AC-1 test ('two same-day fires -> two distinct paths') CAN PASS SPURIOUSLY -- two same-day intraday paths already differ today via the slot component with no hour discriminator at all; the test MUST assert the paths differ IN THE HOUR COMPONENT with the slot component held identical, and must additionally assert the slot component is stable across the two fires; (2) AC-4's audit property ('every non-silent intraday cycle surfaces on disk') stays UNREACHABLE while an auditor cannot deterministically compute the expected path -- which is verbatim the complaint the parent row logged on 2026-07-19; (3) the newer writer ALREADY emits `cycle_vn_hour: 10` as a metadata field, so the hour exists in the artifact and simply never reaches the filename -- bind the filename component to that same pinned value rather than introducing a third derivation. NOT hindsight: the 3 pre-existing `chef-`-prefixed files date from 2026-07-29/07-30, so the variance was observable when this spec was written on 08-08. AC-5 (new): the slot component of the synthesis filename resolves deterministically to ONE convention for a given slot, and an auditor can compute the expected path for any given non-silent cycle from pinned session values alone.

done_tasks.desc:
ROOT CAUSE (re-derived from source, NOT from the reporter's narration). scripts/orch-row-prose-ceiling-check.mjs:114-147 defines STRUCTURAL_FIELDS, the exclude-set of keys that do NOT count toward a row's 'prose bytes'. It already contains `claimed_at` and `claimed_by` — the author correctly understood that a claim stamp is coordination metadata, not prose. But scripts/devteam-review-claim-secondary-drain.jq:135-137 stamps the PREFIXED variants `secondary_claimed_at` / `secondary_claimed_by` / `secondary_dispatch_target`, and none of those three is in the set. They therefore count as prose, the row grows, and orch-row-prose-ceiling-check.mjs:251 (`if (candidateBytes > liveBytes)` on a row already past CEILING_BYTES) hard-rejects the write. orch-apply.sh Stage 2.5 aborts, the live file is untouched, the claim silently no-ops.

WHY IT IS A DETERMINISTIC LIVELOCK, NOT A ONE-ROW PROBLEM. The picker (same file, lines 118-129) is `sort_by(.age) | .[0]` over `age_epoch = .updated_at // .reviewed_at // .created_at` — strictly OLDEST first, with no filter excluding a previously-claimed or previously-failed row. Normally a successful claim bumps the row's updated_at, rotating it to the back of the queue. Here the claim never lands, so updated_at is frozen and the SAME row is re-picked every tick, forever. Confirmed live: SPIKE-BCTC-EXTRACTION-DORMANT-MASS-ENRICHFAIL-FLOOD, review[], updated_at frozen at 2026-08-11T17:36:34Z, 35966B (~3x the 12000B ceiling), no detail_ref. Behind it sit 26 more SECONDARY-eligible rows (27 total: status==REVIEW AND next_agent!=qa), 20 of them never claimed. The whole lane is starved, not just the blocking row.

ONSET IS TODAY, NOT PRE-EXISTING. The guard shipped in 4513c45df at 2026-08-15T04:05:33Z; dev-team reproduced the abort at 06:22:58Z, ~2h17m later. The lane demonstrably drained before that (secondary_claimed_at stamps present on rows dated 08-13 and 08-14, including one at 2026-08-15T05:50:27Z). This is a regression introduced by the guard itself, roughly 3h old at mint time.

WHY THE SHIPPING VERIFICATION MISSED IT. 4513c45df's commit message asserts 'Verified against the real live orch-state.json (read-only + a throwaway copy) to confirm zero regression risk on the next production write: 42 pre-existing over-ceiling rows all resolve to non-blocking WARN, exit 0.' That verification only exercised the STATIC case — rows sitting still. Every over-ceiling row is a non-blocking WARN precisely while nothing writes to it. It never exercised the DYNAMIC case (a claim/drain script stamping an over-ceiling row), which is the only case a live fleet actually produces. Same shape as feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist: the gate was validated on the configuration in which it cannot fail.

FIX (AC-1). Add `secondary_claimed_at`, `secondary_claimed_by`, `secondary_dispatch_target`, and `dispatch_target` to STRUCTURAL_FIELDS in scripts/orch-row-prose-ceiling-check.mjs. This is the root-cause fix and it is ~4 tokens: these are coordination/lifecycle fields by exactly the same argument that already admitted claimed_at/claimed_by, and the file's own comment calls the set a 'Superset of scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh's STUB_FIELDS plus the lifecycle/provenance fields'. Do NOT instead relax the ceiling, add a bypass env var (the guard deliberately has none), or special-case the blocking row.

AC-2 — REGRESSION TEST, the actual deliverable. Add a test that stamps a synthetic OVER-CEILING row with the SECONDARY-Drain field set and asserts exit 0. Without this, AC-1 is a one-line patch with no proof and the next claim script to invent a new stamp field re-opens the identical hole. The test must be dynamic (live-vs-candidate with a mutation), never a static scan.

AC-3 — SCOPE CORRECTION, read before widening. dev-team's report proposed also hardening 'the sibling QA-Drain/BOUNDED-1/SLS/RLC/DRS claim scripts, same stamp-only-growth pattern'. That is an OVERREACH and must not be done: those five are structurally immune, for a reason worth stating so nobody re-widens later. PROSE_CEILING_LANES is exactly ['backlog','ready','review'], and the check only inspects rows present in those lanes in the CANDIDATE document. devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq:171-178 moves review[]->qa[]; devteam-backlog-claim-ready-lane-consumer.jq:142-150, devteam-backlog-claim-bounded1.jq:95-102, devteam-backlog-claim-design-router-sweep.jq:82-89, devteam-backlog-claim-supervised-lane-sweep.jq:148-191 and devteam-claim-backlog-task-by-id.jq:36-41 all move ready[]/backlog[]->in_progress[]. Neither qa[] nor in_progress[] is a guarded lane, so the claimed row leaves the measured set entirely and no violation can fire. devteam-review-claim-secondary-drain.jq is the ONLY claim script that stamps IN PLACE inside a guarded lane (its own header, line 65, says so explicitly: 'stamp ... on the row IN PLACE inside .task_board.review[]'), which is exactly why it is the only one deadlocked. Fixing the exclude-set covers all of them anyway; touching the other five scripts is unnecessary churn.

AC-4 — do NOT adopt the reporter's remedy (a). It proposed migrating SPIKE-BCTC-EXTRACTION-DORMANT-MASS-ENRICHFAIL-FLOOD's prose to detail_ref via scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh to get it back under ceiling. That path is currently BLOCKED by P1 FIX-ORCHBACKLOGSTUB-COLD-ITEMS-ARRAY-SHAPE-CRASH-BLOCKS-LANES-MIGRATION (orch-backlog-stub.sh crashes on the real backlog-detail.json). done_tasks.mechanism: docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md L492 gates the ENTIRE dispatch chain (BOUNDED-1 -> SLS -> RLC -> QA-Drain) on head.status being idle/done/missing/v1. L491 is the only self-heal: 'head.status == in_progress AND head.updated_at >= 24h -> stale crash, reset to idle'. Between those two lines, any head that pins without progressing takes every dispatch lane offline until the 24h timer expires. The Pipeline Resume path at L470-489 does re-spawn head.next_agent each tick, but it stamps nothing on .head, so a spawn that dies before writing anything leaves updated_at frozen and the resume silently repeats — burning one spawn per tick with no forward progress and no alert.

done_tasks.acceptance: (1) A head pinned in_progress with no .head movement AND no commit referencing active_task_id for a bounded interval proportionate to the observed tick cadence (NOT 24h) is detected and reset; PO does not ratify a specific number — architect picks it from the measured cadence and states the basis. (2) Detection emits a BUG-channel signal naming the pinned task id and the pin duration, so a silent spawn failure becomes loud rather than being inferred 4h later from a missing commit. (3) Pipeline Resume records evidence of each re-spawn attempt (e.g. an attempt counter or last_resume_at on .head) so a repeated no-op resume is distinguishable from a task that is genuinely still running — the current state is indistinguishable from the outside, which is why this went unnoticed. (4) Repeated resume of the SAME active_task_id past a small attempt bound stops re-spawning and escalates instead of burning one spawn per tick.

FOUR independent reasons that predicate cannot execute as written, all PO-verified 2026-07-29T02:14-02:25Z. (1) WRONG PATH: the literal jq path .microservices[0].crons resolves to null; the real path is .project.microservices[0].crons (70 entries). Navigable by a human, but wrong as written. (2) SCHEDULE GRAMMAR IS NOT UNIFORM: of the 70 schedules only 32 are parseable 5-field cron expressions. The other 38 (54%) are prose: */15 min, */6h, 08:00 VN M-F, 23:00 VN Sunday, 1st monthly 06:00 VN, 19:00 UTC daily (02:00 VN), plus the two non-schedules startup and helper. Compute-expected-last-fire-from-schedule-expression is undefined for 54% of the inventory. (3) THE NAME JOIN IS BROKEN: get_cron_health returns 87 runtime jobs; system-map lists 70 crons; after aggressive normalization (lowercase, strip trailing Job, strip non-alphanumerics) only 48 join. 39 runtime jobs have NO system-map entry and therefore no schedule and are uncheckable by this predicate at all, including pollNews, pollNews_all_sources_dark, bondMaturityPoller, publicContracts, vnstockFundamentalsRefresh, deepFetchMain, deepFetchVps, schedulerWatchdog, restartCadenceAlert and diskUsageAlert. 22 system-map crons have NO runtime record. Runtime names carry a Job suffix and :variant suffixes (dataAuditJob:daily, marketScanJob:open) that the SSOT names do not; no mapping contract exists. (4) NO DATA SOURCE FOR CLAUDE-CODE CRONS: systemAuditTier1/2/3 ARE present in .project.microservices[0].crons with clean parseable schedules (*/30 * * * *, 0 */4 * * *, 0 2 * * *) but are ABSENT from get_cron_health because they are Claude Code CronCreate crons, not mcp-server node-cron jobs. They land in the 22-cron no-runtime-record bucket and are silently skipped. WHAT THE CYCLE ACTUALLY RAN INSTEAD: Cron Health (A-29): 127+ jobs tracked; all success_rate >=80%, majority >=99% - PASS. The strings success_rate and 80% appear NOWHERE in docs/agents/system-auditor/ (PO re-ran the grep and confirms zero hits) - the bar is agent-invented and re-chosen per cycle, so A-29 is also non-reproducible. WHY THE SUBSTITUTE IS WORSE THAN NOTHING: success_rate is a ratio over runs that HAPPENED. A cron that stopped firing retains its historical ratio forever - a dead cron reports ~99% and PASSES. The substitute cannot detect a stopped cron under any circumstance, which is precisely and only the failure mode A-29 exists to catch.

MINTED 2026-07-25T16:25:39Z by po (router triage input, RAW-verified at source by po before minting — every number below was measured this tick, none relayed).

THE DEFECT IS NOT INACCURATE BOOKKEEPING — IT IS A TRIGGER THE WRITER MAKES UNSATISFIABLE.
Read contract, docs/agents/news-scout/flow/stage-sentiment.md:16-21 — STALE_TICKERS = watchlist tickers where last_covered_news_scout == null OR (now - last_covered) > 48h, sorted oldest-first, take <=3 per cycle. Write contract, docs/agents/news-scout/flow/stage-log-notify.md:62-63 — "for each ticker analyzed this cycle (both event-driven AND sweep-forced): set .tickers[t].last_covered_news_scout = now". The write contract is CORRECT AS WRITTEN. The execution is not: every cycle stamps ALL tickers, so no ticker can ever age past 48h, STALE_TICKERS is permanently empty, and the <=3-per-cycle rotation can never fire. The sweep is the only mechanism guaranteeing periodic coverage of low-news watchlist tickers; it has been the equivalent of disabled.

MEASURED (docs/data/coverage-state.json, .tickers has 57 entries):
  - after the 16:14Z tick: all 57 carry the byte-identical stamp 2026-07-25T16:14:39Z (jq group_by -> ONE group, n=57).
  - previous committed version: all 57 carry the byte-identical stamp 2026-07-25T12:10:42Z (ONE group, n=57).
  - the 16:14Z cycle (c200) analyzed 2 tickers by its own evidence trail: fragments #584 VNM and #585 MARKET. Not 57.
  - COVERAGE COST, the reason this is P1: ~2 of 57 tickers get event-driven coverage per cycle. The other ~55 are reachable ONLY via the sweep. With the sweep alive (<=3/cycle, ~6 cycles/day) full rotation completes in ~3.2 days; with it dead the long tail gets zero scheduled coverage indefinitely.

SCOPE IS DOUBLE WHAT THE INPUT REPORTED — MARKET-WATCHER HAS THE IDENTICAL DEFECT, LIVE.
The triage input named only news-scout. po checked the sibling field in the same file and it is equally saturated: all 57 tickers carry byte-identical last_covered_market_watcher = 2026-07-25T08:10:06Z. market-watcher's flow carries the same pair of contracts in the same shape — read at docs/agents/market-watcher/flow/cycle.md:60-73, write at :240-250 ("for each ticker priced this cycle (both anomaly-driven AND sweep-forced)"). Any fix that touches only news-scout leaves half the defect live. BOTH agents are in scope; this is stated here because a narrow reading of the originating report would miss it.

THE BEHAVIOUR IS INTERMITTENT, NOT A CLEAN REGRESSION — DO NOT CHASE A BREAKING COMMIT.
po walked 25 historical revisions of the file. Distinct-stamp counts for last_covered_news_scout: 3/4/7 on 06-30, then 1 across 07-02..07-21, then 5 at 819fff993 (07-23, correct shape: a 38-ticker fossil group at 07-21T16:14 plus small 2/2/4/11 groups from later cycles), then 1/1 on 07-25. last_covered_market_watcher: 8,9,10,10,10,6,7,11 through 07-23, then 1,1 on 07-25. So BOTH agents have produced correct per-ticker stamping at some points and blanket stamping at others, with no code change in between. THAT IS THE ROOT CAUSE AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT: the write is a prose instruction executed by an LLM against a 57-entry JSON blob, so faithfulness is non-deterministic per cycle. Editing the prose to say it more emphatically is NOT a fix — the prose is already correct. The fix must move the write to a deterministic scripted surgical patch.

INDEPENDENT PROOF THE WRITE IS A FULL-DOC OVERWRITE, NOT A MERGE — A TOP-LEVEL CONFIG KEY WAS SILENTLY DELETED.
coverage-state.json had a top-level sweep_config block ({max_staleness_hours: 48, sweep_batch_size: 3}) — present at 0866c35b6 (2026-07-21), ABSENT from 819fff993 (2026-07-23) onward, and absent live today. Nothing deleted it deliberately; a hand-rewrite of the blob dropped it. Corroborated by docs/handoffs/2026-07-16-coverage-state-cross-agent-lost-update-and-three-premise-corrections.md:16, which enumerates the then-current top-level keys including sweep_config, and by docs/data/.trash/2026-07-20/docs/archive/coverage-state.json.tmp:67 which still carries it. CONSEQUENCE, fold into this fix: BOTH flow docs still cite "sweep_config.sweep_batch_size" (stage-sentiment.md:21, cycle.md:73) against a key that no longer exists — a dangling config reference. It is currently harmless only because the prose also hardcodes "<=3" next to it, and max_staleness_hours=48 now survives solely as prose in two files. Restore the block (or relocate the two constants to a real config surface) as part of this row; do NOT mint a separate row for it.

CO-SHIP — THIS ROW AND FIX-COVERAGE-STATE-CROSS-AGENT-LOST-UPDATE ARE ONE CHANGE, NOT TWO.
That row (backlog/P2/M/plan_only, minted 2026-07-16) records the same file being clobbered on the _ssot blob across agents, and its candidate direction (i) reads "serialize the two writers behind a shared coverage-state write helper that does read-modify-merge (not full-doc overwrite)". This row is direct corroboration that (i) is correct and that the live write IS a full-doc overwrite — the vanished sweep_config key is the proof that row was missing. One helper satisfies both ACs; shipping them separately means editing the same write step in the same two flow files twice, with the second edit racing the first. Sequence: this row leads (P1, live coverage loss), the lost-update row closes with it and its AC 1 becomes AC 3 below.

ROUTED DIRECT TO developer, NOT ba, DELIBERATELY. The sibling row was minted plan_only/next_agent=ba on 2026-07-16 because its direction was genuinely open between three candidates. That question is now CLOSED by the sweep_config deletion evidence above, which is the discriminating observation that row lacked. What remains is one shell script, its test, and two flow-doc edits against a fully specified AC — that is a direct FIX, and holding a P1 live-coverage-loss behind a planning hop for a settled design would be disproportionate. The implementer MUST NOT re-open the direction; if implementation reveals the direction is wrong after all, bounce the row back to po with the contradicting evidence rather than re-scoping in place.

REMEDY SHAPE (direction settled, details open to ba/architect):
Replace the prose read-modify-write in BOTH flow files with one deterministic script — proposed scripts/agents-flow/coverage-stamp.sh, invoked as `coverage-stamp.sh --agent <news-scout|market-watcher> --tickers VNM,FPT` — that does a surgical jq patch of ONLY the named tickers, preserves every other key byte-for-byte, and holds a short mutex (task_claim "coverage-state:main", TTL ~30s) around the read-modify-write. This is exactly the shape already proposed and left unbuilt as cowork-cycle-agents-P10 in docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-12-ultracode-workflow-improvement-audit.md:982-986 — that proposal is UNVERIFIED-status there and is hereby superseded by this row, which carries the live evidence it lacked. Genuinely open for the implementer, and the only open question on this row: whether the script also emits the STALE_TICKERS list (so the read side becomes deterministic too, closing the same class on the read path) or only owns the write.

ACCEPTANCE (biconditional — a one-directional test cannot distinguish this fix from the current behaviour):
  1. POSITIVE: after a cycle that analyses N tickers, EXACTLY those N carry the new stamp; `jq '[.tickers|to_entries[]|.value.last_covered_news_scout]|group_by(.)|length'` returns > 1 whenever N < 57. Same assertion for last_covered_market_watcher.
  2. NEGATIVE (this is the one that actually proves the trigger is alive): seed a ticker with a stamp older than 48h, run a cycle, and assert it appears in STALE_TICKERS and is force-included. A test that only checks "the right tickers got stamped" passes today for a 57-ticker cycle and proves nothing.
  3. PRESERVATION: after the write, every top-level key present before the write is still present (regression test for the sweep_config deletion class) and the peer agent's last_covered_* field is unchanged (this is the lost-update row's AC 1).
  4. Both agents covered. A fix landing on news-scout only does not close this row.

SECONDARY OBSERVATION, ONE LINE FOR WHOEVER WORKS THIS — DO NOT EXPAND SCOPE: three unreconciled ticker counts. coverage-state.json has 57 entries; news-scout's c200 notebook asserts "all 58 watchlist sweep"; docs/data/system-map.json's watchlist node has 34. The sweep iterates WATCHLIST (from the get_watchlist tool) but stamps and reads the FILE, so a ticker present in one and not the other is either never swept or never stamped. po did NOT determine which count is authoritative — flag it in the fix's findings, do not silently pick one.

What Bash genuinely adds over Write+Edit is process execution and network egress (`git push`, `docker`, curl) — real, and the reason this is a considered grant rather than a rubber stamp, but not the step-change in capability class that would justify blocking a live P1 behind a rewrite.

done_tasks.title: Ready-Lane Consumer has no severity/incident expedite path: inside one priority class the tiebreak is the ready[] array index, so a P0 minted for a LIVE production incident lands at the back of a 78-deep queue and is unreachable in incident time
done_tasks.desc: MEASURED, not inferred. Replaying scripts/devteam-backlog-claim-ready-lane-consumer.jq 14 successive times against a live copy of the board on 2026-08-12T05:36Z put FIX-RAG-EMBEDDER-IDLE-UNLOAD-ALLOCATOR-PAGES-NOT-RETURNED-TO-OS — a P0 for a service that was OOM-cycling every ~50 minutes and had taken 3 emergency ops restarts in 90 minutes — at pick #8. It sits at ready[] index 76 of 78 and is the LAST of 26 P0 rows in the lane. RLC's documented selection is 'ordered by priority_rank ascending, tiebreak by ready[] array index (FIFO proxy)'; a row minted today is always appended, so recency and severity are anti-correlated with dispatch order inside a priority class. Compounding factors, both live-verified: RLC claims exactly ONE row per invocation (its own header: 'single row per invocation'), and it only runs when it wins the 6-way idle-chain rotation (.dev_team_idle_chain.rotation shows all 6 candidates served ~30min apart, i.e. ~3h per lane, against cron `7,37 * * * *`). Every pick must additionally satisfy wip_in_progress < 2. Floor-bound expected latency for the tail of the P0 class is ~24h and realistically days. PO had to hand-dispatch out of band, which is a producer-with-no-mechanism escape hatch, not a designed path.
done_tasks.scope: Design an expedite/severity dimension for ready-lane selection that does NOT simply add a 4th priority tier (P0 is already saturated at 26 rows — a new tier saturates the same way). Candidate shapes for the architect to adjudicate, none pre-selected: (a) an explicit, PO-settable `expedite_at` / `incident_ref` field that sorts ahead of priority_rank and is bounded to N rows so it cannot itself saturate; (b) age-weighted or arrival-inverted tiebreak inside a priority class so a fresh incident row is not structurally last; (c) a separate low-cardinality incident lane with its own budget, outside the shared WIP<=2 slot and outside the 6-way rotation, mirroring how QA-Drain already carries an independent qa[] budget for structurally different work. Any design MUST keep the existing single-linear head-writer collision-freedom proof intact (docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-29-qadrain-head-slot-decouple.md).

That names no concrete surface. Re-confirm it live before writing it into the doc as fact.

DEFECT (b) — THE MARKERS ARE SELF-INJECTED, AND THE SPEC'S OWN JUSTIFICATION FOR THEM IS FACTUALLY WRONG. This part IS PO-verified by measurement and does not depend on (a). spawn-fanout.md:374-375 sets OFFFLOW_MARKERS = ['Coordination Results','Dispatch Routing','PRE-CLAIM','session-presence','orphan-adoption','Expected Behavior'] and :376 justifies them as 'Verbatim section headings / terms from the project-root CLAUDE.md router dispatch protocol.'   global  CLAUDE.md  : all six = 0

That preamble is prepended to EVERY spawn's entry prompt. The detector therefore greps for a string list that the dispatcher guarantees is present in every spawn's own prompt, by construction. Combined with the 3 markers CLAUDE.md injects into every agent's context, ANY extraction surface that includes the prompt or the transcript matches 6/6 unconditionally — the symlink in (a) is one such surface, not the root cause.

done_tasks.note:
PO TRIAGE 2026-07-21 (TNB c115 finding F-CHEF-MORNING-FALSE-FULL-VERDICT). VERDICT: CONFIRMED AT SOURCE by PO — with ONE correction to TNB's evidence chain (below). This is a FALSE CERTIFICATION, which is a strictly worse failure mode than every previously-tracked chef finding: all prior ones were HONEST degraded self-reports.

RAW EVIDENCE (PO read docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-morning.json directly; note the fields are NESTED — metadata.* and tnb_synthesis.* — a top-level jq query returns null and will look like a missing field):
- metadata.cycle_id = "morning-2026-07-21T05:20:19Z"
- metadata.quality_verdict = "full"
- metadata.layers_walked_summary = "1-6 (full)"
- tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer = "Fed funds rate 3.63% with risk-off sentiment signaled by gold spike +$24.1 to $4053/oz. Safe-haven demand reflects caution amid margin debt expansion."  -> Fed funds ONLY. NO PMI. NO EFFR-IORB spread. Both are mandatory Layer-2 content per tnb-methodology.md / the main.md Layer table.
- known_gaps = ["[gap:business_context_sparse] ...", "[gap:gold_4300_active] ..."] -> ZERO L2 gap token.
So the dish certifies 6/6 layers walked while its own persisted payload shows Layer 2 is not walked, and emits no gap token to compensate. The quality signal is not merely wrong, it is confidently wrong — downstream consumers that trust quality_verdict to gate use have no way to detect this.

*** CORRECTION TO TNB'S EVIDENCE (PO re-verified; do not carry TNB's version forward) ***
TNB's finding argues the self-scoring gate CAN work by contrasting the SAME-DAY eod dish, which it says "explicitly tokens [gap:L2_US_macro_absent]". That contrast is NOT RAW-verifiable: docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-eod.json DOES NOT EXIST (PO ls-confirmed; TNB's OWN other finding, GAP-CHEF-SYNTHESIS-A-FLOW-PERSIST, states the same file is Glob-confirmed absent). TNB therefore cited the eod NOTEBOOK claim as if it were persisted-JSON evidence, in the same handoff where it correctly reports that JSON never landed — an internal contradiction.
The proof leg SURVIVES, but must be re-anchored to the EVENING dish, which PO verified RAW: unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-evening.json has metadata.quality_verdict="degraded" AND tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer="EFFR-IORB spread 1.64pp NEUTRAL. Brent +2.31% ... Gold +1.97% ..." — i.e. genuine L2 content and an honest verdict, same agent, same day. That is a sound same-day control and it establishes the same point: the defect is isolated to the morning cycle, not universal.
CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS: do not build the fix around a comparison with the eod JSON. It is not there.

OCCURRENCE COUNT = 1 (first live-verified). Below the 3-cycle auto-cure threshold, and PO agrees auto-cure is the WRONG instrument here regardless of count — see the sibling row below.

FIX SHAPE (PO directive): the verdict gate must be a DETERMINISTIC ASSERTION, not a narrative self-judgement. Before writing metadata.quality_verdict="full", the agent must assert per-layer that the layer's own payload field is non-empty AND contains its mandatory tokens (L2: PMI and/or EFFR-IORB). If an assertion fails, "full" is not writable — the verdict must downgrade to "degraded" and a [gap:L<N>_...] token must be appended to known_gaps. Verdict and gap-token must be derived from ONE evaluation so they cannot disagree.

AC: (1) quality_verdict="full" is unwritable when any mandatory layer field lacks its required tokens; (2) verdict and known_gaps are computed from a single pass (no independent second judgement); (3) negative control — a synthetic dish with L2 stripped must produce degraded + an L2 gap token, proving the assertion fires (without this the fix is indistinguishable from always writing degraded); (4) RAW-verify on the next morning fire by reading metadata.quality_verdict + tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer from the persisted JSON — an agent self-report or notebook line is NOT acceptable evidence (the 07-21 morning notebook line matched the false "full" verbatim, so the notebook faithfully reproduces the bad verdict and cannot detect it).

SIBLING / DO NOT MERGE: FIX-CHEF-L6-TOKEN-PERSISTENCE-RECURRING (P3, BLOCKED) is the nearest prior art and is RELATED BUT DISTINCT. That row = a token WAS generated and then dropped on JSON write (persist-step vs narrative-gen, isolation-first, 3 manifestations despite 2 auto-cures). THIS row = no token was ever generated AND the verdict was affirmatively certified "full". Different mechanism, opposite end of the pipeline. They share the family "chef self-scoring integrity" and should be looked at together, but merging them would bury a false-certification bug inside a persistence bug. The L6 row's own lesson applies here though: more same-shape auto-cure is the wrong move; this needs a deterministic assertion.

P0 CI-BLOCKING. Second of the two jobs red on origin/main 429dcf8fa (run 32645643303, job agent-bash-grant-coverage 97209377297). Reproduced locally on this HEAD — genuinely red, not stale.

DEFECT (measured, not inferred): scripts/audits/agent-bash-grant-coverage.sh:103 sets DEMAND_ERE='bash scripts/|git add|git commit|git push|commit-mutex|commit-boundary' and greps it over the agent's whole flow corpus with no negation handling. Commit baa91292c ('chore(agents): fleet-wide debug-logger-protocol rollout (Check #6)') added this boilerplate note to agent init.md knowledge blocks fleet-wide:
  note: "Per-agent debug logger convention. Append one line to docs/agent-memory/debug/<id>.log per notable step/error (Read-then-Write append, no MCP tool, no per-line git commit)."
The substring 'git commit' inside 'no per-line git commit' matches DEMAND_ERE. The sentence says the OPPOSITE of a Bash demand — it explicitly prescribes Read-then-Write and forbids per-line git commit.

EVIDENCE THIS IS A PURE FP, NOT REAL DEBT: ran `find docs/agents/refine_bctc_md -name '*.md' | xargs grep -niE '<DEMAND_ERE>'` — EXACTLY ONE match across the entire corpus (init.md:80), and it is that negated sentence. refine_bctc_md's corpus references one skill (.claude/skills/bctc-gate-vision/SKILL.md) with no match either. There is no real Bash-only step anywhere in this agent's flow.

DO NOT FIX BY GRANTING BASH. Granting Bash to refine_bctc_md would silence CI by laundering a detector bug into a genuine privilege escalation on a deliberately Bash-less agent. DO NOT FIX BY BASELINING EITHER: docs/data/agent-bash-grant-coverage-baseline.json is documented in-script as a ledger of real-but-separately-owned debt, explicitly NOT an opt-out allowlist, and requires a non-null owning_task — there is no real debt here to own.

CORRECT FIX (developer's call between these): (a) make the demand match negation-aware — reject a DEMAND_ERE hit preceded on the same line by 'no ' / 'never ' / 'without ' / 'not '; or (b) exclude YAML `note:`/`description:` scalar values inside the frontmatter knowledge block from the corpus scan, since those are prose-about-tooling not flow steps; or (c) require the match to be in an executable position (fenced code block or a step line), not inside a quoted YAML string. (a) is narrowest, (c) is most durable. Whichever is chosen, add a regression fixture containing the exact debug-logger boilerplate string.

BLAST RADIUS — this will recur: the boilerplate is fleet-wide, so EVERY Bash-less agent that receives it reds this gate. Only refine_bctc_md trips today (bctc-analyst is already baselined under FIX-BCTC-ANALYST-STAGELOG-NOTIFY-NO-BASH — check whether that baseline entry is the same FP and should be retired by this fix rather than left as fake debt). Any future Bash-less agent onboarded with the standard note reds CI on arrival.

done_tasks.question: owner:null + next_agent:null is a LEGITIMATE documented state (zone-routing.md Step A2 row 4: 'genuinely parked, no handler yet' -> consumed by nothing, intentional). So the invariant is NOT 'every row needs a handler'. DECIDE the enforcement point — (1) non-fatal REPORT stage in scripts/orch-validate.mjs alongside the existing Stage-1g dangling-dependency report, (2) a superRefine in apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/orchStateSchema.ts (fatal — check the live blast radius first, this WILL reject writes), or (3) auto-derive next_agent from zone at mint time. Both contract_status values that can force DETECTED on a non-zero-diff cycle are computed from `_plane_output_contract_claims()`, which extracts the `[OUTPUT-CONTRACT]` line via `git log -p -- "$notebook_path"`. done_tasks.desc: USER-REPORTED 2026-08-23 (verbatim intent: 'no all session is running actual but status not update'). Section 'Cron phiên làm việc (23)' on http://localhost:3001/dashboard/orchestration renders, for ALL 23 rows: Lần chạy gần nhất = 'Chưa từng chạy', Dự kiến lần tới = '—', Trạng thái = 'Phiên làm việc'. === NOT A TRACKING OUTAGE, NOT A CRON FAILURE === The crons ARE running. 'Chưa từng chạy' is a constant by construction and can never say anything else: (1) apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/cron/layerBCronRegistry.ts builds Layer-B rows by PARSING .claude/commands/crons/*.md authoring docs on disk. It is a static config-catalogue read; it never queries any runtime fire table. Its `interface CronStatusRowB` types `expected_last_fire`/`expected_next_fire`/`last_fire`/`last_status` as the LITERAL type `null` (not `string | null`), and `buildRow()` hardcodes all four to null + `status: "SESSION_SCOPED"`. It is type-level impossible for a Layer-B row to ever carry a fire timestamp. This is CORRECT and deliberate — CronCreate jobs live inside the Claude Code CLI process, which has no writer into market.db, so there is no Layer-B equivalent of Layer-A's getDistinctJobNames(db)+buildLayerARow(...) telemetry pipeline in cronStatusHandler.ts. done_tasks.title: server-reaper mints orphan-signals keyed ONLY on lock TTL expiry with ZERO liveness check — gcExpiredLocks' Phase-1 scan never consults session-presence, so a presence-REGISTERED, demonstrably-live session's long-running task is falsely orphaned the moment its TTL lapses
done_tasks.desc:
CONFIRMED AT SOURCE by po triage 2026-08-25T01:07Z (session 036ceaf1) — read verbatim from the implementation, NOT inferred from the signal. Two dev-team recurring-bug envelopes (d89d8226 and its correction 4a5a8e12, carrying corrects_envelope_id) collapse to ONE finding; envelope 2 supersedes envelope 1's root cause and ONLY envelope 2's premise is built on here.

THE PREDICATE (apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/db/coordinationStore.ts, gcExpiredLocks() Phase 1 pre-GC scan):
  WHERE expires_at + ? < unixepoch('now')
    AND task_kind IN (ORPHAN_EMIT_ALLOW_LIST)
    AND task_id NOT LIKE 'published:%'
    AND task_id NOT LIKE 'cron:%'
    AND task_id NOT LIKE 'cron-registration:%'
    AND task_id != 'dev-team-cron-singleton'
TTL expiry is the SOLE liveness proxy. The row's own owner_client_session IS selected by that query — but only to be copied into the emitted signal payload as original_owner_client_session. It is never used to ask whether that session is still alive. There is no join, no subquery and no lookup against task_kind='session-presence' anywhere in the function.

LIVE EVIDENCE: orphan-signal:task:FIX-CHEF-BIZCTX-GATHER-TO-CONVICTION-WIRING was minted 2026-08-24T23:59:49Z against a lock owned by session 036ceaf1-bf34-46cd-92e4-8c6b213ff4bb — a session that was presence-REGISTERED and LIVE at mint time (started_at 2026-08-24T21:09:38Z, heartbeat_at 2026-08-25T01:09:58Z, continuously running, executed ticks 00:37Z / 00:54Z / 01:07Z) and was still live when this row was written. Observed re-trips of the same false orphan: 00:37Z and 01:07Z.

WHY ENVELOPE 1'S FRAMING IS INSUFFICIENT (deliberately NOT built on): 'the S2 dispatch convention leaves the sprint-task lock unreleased on the success path' is a real contributing factor but NOT the generator. A fix designed against it would leave the defect fully intact for any task that legitimately outlives its TTL — the reaper would still falsely orphan a correctly-behaving, mid-flight, long-running agent.

CRITICAL DESIGN CONSTRAINT — THE GUARD MUST BE SUPPRESS-ONLY, NEVER ASSERT-DEAD. Sibling row SPIKE-SESSION-PRESENCE-ROSTER-UNDERCOUNTS-LIVE-SESSIONS (backlog, P2) measured task_list_held(kind=session-presence) returning 1 row while >=3 sessions were demonstrably live, and presence registration is OPT-IN, so an ABSENT presence row does NOT mean the session is dead. Required polarity: presence row PRESENT and unexpired => SUPPRESS the mint; presence ABSENT => fall through to exactly today's behaviour. Under that polarity an undercounting roster can only make the guard weaker, never wrong — which is why this row deliberately does NOT depend_on the SPIKE and must not be blocked behind it.

CHEAP TO IMPLEMENT: session-presence rows live in the SAME task_locks table (task_kind='session-presence'), so the guard is one NOT EXISTS correlated subquery added to the existing Phase-1 SELECT — same transaction, no new I/O, no new table, no schema change.

DO NOT COPY THE CRON STEP 1b.1 ORACLE VERBATIM: envelope 2 proposes mirroring the oracle in .claude/skills/cron-detect-loop/SKILL.md Step 1b.1. Open row FIX-CRON-REARM-STEP1B1-LIVENESS-ORACLE-BLIND-WINDOW-FALSE-LIVE (ready[], P0) documents at source that that oracle is broken in BOTH directions across 3 cron families and cost an 8h10m dispatcher outage on 2026-08-23. Take the SHAPE (cross-check presence before acting on lock state); never that implementation.

done_tasks.title: auditor-tier1-probe.test.sh:1422 T-DEBOUNCE-1 last_seen_at assertion is INVERTED — uses `|| echo true` where all 263 sibling assertions use `&& echo true || echo false`, so it records FAIL when the ledger is CORRECT and PASS when it is BROKEN; FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-SPAWN-DEBOUNCE-1-PROBE-SCRIPT was approved on a 264/264 run that passed only because of this inversion
done_tasks.root_cause: check() (same file, L30-39) increments PASS only when its second argument is the literal string "true". The 263 sibling assertions build that argument as `$([ COND ] && echo true || echo false)`, which yields "true"/"false". Line 1422 alone builds it as `$([ A != B ] || echo true)`: when the timestamps DIFFER (the condition the label asserts, and the healthy behaviour) the test succeeds, `||` short-circuits, nothing is echoed, the substitution is the empty string, and check() records FAIL. When the timestamps are IDENTICAL (the broken behaviour) `echo true` runs and check() records PASS. The assertion therefore tests the exact negation of its own label.

done_tasks.title: notebook-auto-prune.sh emits structurally malformed signal JSON whenever a section count is zero — `grep -c ... || echo 0` double-emits at 5 sites, and both currently-malformed files in the signal inbox come from this one bug
done_tasks.desc: REPRODUCED DIRECTLY THIS TICK, not inferred. The idiom `VAR="$(... | grep -c PATTERN 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"` is wrong for `grep -c`: on zero matches grep -c PRINTS its own `0` to stdout AND exits 1, so the `|| echo 0` fallback also fires and the capture becomes the two-line string "0\n0". Verified by direct repro: `X=$(grep -c NOMATCH file || echo 0); echo "[$X]"` yields `[0` / `0]`. When that value is interpolated into the emitted signal JSON the document is corrupted. LIVE WIRE EVIDENCE: docs/signals/notebook-prune-dropped-newest-docs-agent-memory-notebooks-dev-mcp-server-md-2026-08-22T232534Z.json line 13 reads `"sentinel_section_count": 0` and line 14 is a bare `0,`. `jq .` on that file fails with `parse error: Expected separator between values at line 14, column 2`. AFFECTED SITES (all in scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh): 477 SECTION_COUNT, 518 SECTION_COUNT, 574 NON_SENTINEL_SECTION_COUNT, 575 SENTINEL_SECTION_COUNT, 601 TIE_COUNT. BLAST RADIUS MEASURED: scanning every docs/signals/*.json this tick, exactly 2 files are invalid JSON and BOTH are notebook-prune-dropped-newest-* files from this writer — i.e. 100% of the signal inbox's malformed-JSON population is produced by this one defect. Those files never reach isDrainableShape() at all, so they are permanently undrainable and invisible to the drain path's own accounting.
acceptance: AC-1: All 5 sites corrected so a zero count yields the single character `0`. `grep -c` already prints 0 on no-match, so the `|| echo 0` fallback is redundant for the no-match case; it is only needed for a genuine grep ERROR (exit 2). Preferred shape: `VAR="$(... | grep -c PATTERN 2>/dev/null)" || VAR=0` — capture first, default only on non-zero exit, then normalize.

AC-2: Regression test that drives the zero-match path on each of the 5 sites and asserts the emitted signal file parses under `jq .`. Asserting the variable equals "0" is NOT sufficient — the observable defect is malformed JSON on disk.

AC-3: The 2 existing malformed files in docs/signals/ are repaired or removed as part of this fix, and a rerun of the full-inbox scan (`for f in docs/signals/*.json; do jq . "$f" >/dev/null || echo INVALID; done`) reports zero invalid files.
AC-4: Negative control — a NON-zero section count still emits valid JSON with the correct number, proving the fix did not simply hardcode 0.
non_goals: Do NOT touch scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.js, isDrainableShape(), isByPathConsumerFamilies(), or the price_anomaly_* files — all owned by FIX-SIGNAL-INBOX-NON-DRAINABLE-ENVELOPE-50-OF-51-FILES-SILENTLY-CLASSED-LITTER and its brief, which deliberately scoped this writer OUT.
Do not widen the prune logic itself; this is a quoting/exit-code defect only.

done_tasks.root_cause: docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:167-171, clause 4 of the A-30 Memory Reclamation Discriminator block shipped by FIX-AUDITOR-A12A20A30-FP-REEMIT-CONVERGE (2026-07-23, DONE, commit 2f956f1c5): 'if verdict=="ESCALATE" AND vmhwm_kb and vmrss_kb are both numeric AND vmhwm_kb > vmrss_kb -> downgrade to PASS, no emit'. DEFECT 1 — TAUTOLOGY: VmHWM is /proc/<pid>/status's peak-resident-set high-water mark and is monotonically non-decreasing over process lifetime; VmRSS is instantaneous. Therefore VmHWM >= VmRSS holds by construction, and VmHWM > VmRSS is FALSE only in the knife-edge instant where current RSS equals the all-time peak. The predicate carries approximately zero information about memory safety: it answers 'has this process ever freed a page', never 'where does the peak sit relative to the cap'. Three router-captured samples on the SAME mcp-server container 2026-07-25, all three vetoing identically: 12:38Z (auditor's own pre-swap sample) VmHWM 2851248kB / VmRSS 2841768kB, ~93% of the 3GiB cap -> VmHWM>VmRSS TRUE -> PASS; 12:42:26Z (router, pre-swap) VmHWM 3084864kB = 98.1% OF CAP / VmRSS 2949772kB = 93.28% -> TRUE -> PASS; 12:47:46Z (router, post-swap 3-minute-old container) VmHWM 327700kB = 10.4% of cap / VmRSS 311208kB = 10.79% -> TRUE -> would PASS. Identical verdict at 98.1% of cap and at 10.4% of cap. DEFECT 1b — SIGN IS ARGUABLY INVERTED near the cap: a WIDER VmHWM-minus-VmRSS gap on a process close to its limit simultaneously proves the process has already touched an even higher fraction of the cap (12:42:26Z: the very reading the clause reads as reassurance is the reading that shows a 98.1%-of-cap peak). DEFECT 2 — PRECEDENCE: clause 4 is written to run BEFORE clause 5's verdict/reason mapping, so it pre-empts ALL of clause 5, including `verdict==ESCALATE` + reason `OOMKilled=true` -> CRITICAL and `peak >97%` -> CRITICAL. A container that was genuinely OOM-killed and restarted presents a fresh process whose VmHWM > VmRSS almost immediately, so the confirmed-OOM CRITICAL branch is reachable in practice only when VM data is UNAVAILABLE. (A) The CONFIDENCE-GATED path — AutoFallbackOcrBackend, selected by OCR_TEXT_BACKEND=auto, described at apps/pdf-extractor/main.py as 'Tesseract-first; PaddleOCR on low confidence'. That is the mechanism this row measured and falsified. RETIRED as the rescue trigger. Its sibling DECISION-PDFX-OCR-TEXT-BACKEND-DEFAULT-FLIP-TO-AUTO is already CANCELLED in archive[], which is consistent. (B) The CHARACTER-COUNT path — apps/pdf-extractor/infrastructure/ocr_worker.py:455-495, which fires the PaddleOCR(lang=vi) rescue when a page yields fewer than LOW_TESSERACT_PAGE_CHARS and then keeps whichever output is longer. This is a DIFFERENT and far more robust discriminator: it does not need to distinguish 'broken' from 'legitimate-but-sparse' at all, because it only ever ADDS text and keeps the better of two results, so a false fire costs latency and never costs correctness. It is already shipped and it is the sanctioned bounded-rescue path. That asymmetry is exactly why (A) failed and (B) does not: (A) must classify, (B) only has to compare.
