market-db-journal-guard: the BUG alert channel is structurally dead for the exact duration of
every outage it is built to report -- demonstrated live, 7/7 alerts undelivered across a ~74-min
CRITICAL mcp-server outage on 2026-08-25 (approx 05:31Z -> 06:45Z). Plus two probe-robustness
defects in the same script that the existing P2 row does NOT cover.

DEFECT 1 (the important one) -- ALERT CHANNEL DEAD EXACTLY WHEN NEEDED. The cron's exit-2/exit-3
branch alerts via call_tool(server="vn-market", tool="send_telegram"). send_telegram EXECUTES ON
THE mcp-server CONTAINER. So whenever mcp-server is down -- which is precisely the condition that
makes the probe emit exit 3 -- the alert transport is down too. Every alert this guard exists to
raise is undeliverable at the moment it fires. This is not a flaky-transport problem; it is a
topology problem, and it is self-cancelling by construction.
  EVIDENCE, not inference: ticks 1-7 of 2026-08-25 each attempted exactly one send_telegram per
  contract. All 7 failed ("The socket connection was closed unexpectedly."). The user was never
  notified of a CRITICAL fleet outage through the intended channel by ANY tick. The outage was
  ultimately resolved by host action, not by any alert this system delivered.
  The 7 verdict lines are permanently lost: the cron contract forbids reconstructing a verdict
  line from memory, so they cannot be replayed after recovery either.
  SHAPE OF FIX IS A DESIGN QUESTION, NOT PRESCRIBED HERE -- an out-of-band transport that does

STRUCTURAL DEFECT (primary). scripts/db-integrity-history-append.sh is the sole actuator for the

a deterministic script actuator, precisely because prose-only enforcement had let the SAME residue
be re-signalled 3x. But the verdict LABEL ITSELF was left as free LLM judgment with no binding to
the evidence. So anything an agent labels BY-DESIGN / NOISE / CLEAN is invisible to dedup-check,
invisible to the signal write, and invisible to every enforcement path in the cron -- while still
being recorded in the durable history trail as an inspected, dispositioned finding. The hardening
is bypassable by a one-word choice, and the bypass leaves no trace that a bypass occurred.

CONCRETE INSTANCE (how it surfaced). The 07:00:48Z sweep labelled the 336-row daily_ohlcv OHLC
violation residue verdict="BY-DESIGN", signal_id=null. That skipped the actuator. Router then
scanned for an owner and found NONE.

and either attach it to an existing row or mint one. NOT ATTRIBUTING BAD FAITH to the sweep -- it

orch-apply.sh:172 builds a NON-RANDOMIZED temp filename on macOS, so concurrent writes to the fleet-mandated orch-state.json path hard-collide. | MECHANISM, reproduced not inferred: the template is `mktemp "$(dirname "$LIVE_FILE")/.orch-apply-XXXXXXXX.json"`. BSD/macOS mktemp only substitutes the X run when it is at the END of the template; with the `.json` suffix after it, mktemp creates the LITERAL file `.orch-apply-XXXXXXXX.json`. Control in the same shell: `mktemp ./ctrl-XXXXXXXX` twice -> ctrl-SMwiwaJE, ctrl-NQ9Zpalc (randomized); `mktemp ./.orch-apply-XXXXXXXX.json` twice -> first OK, second `mkstemp failed: File exists`. GNU mktemp tolerates a suffix, which is why this is macOS-specific and why it never showed up in CI. | OBSERVED LIVE this tick: dev-team 18:37Z drain, first `drain-signals.js` run aborted twice with `mkstemp failed ... File exists` while 3 subagents were running concurrently (one of them, system-auditor, writes signal rows through the same wrapper). The mv is still atomic and a losing caller gets a clean non-zero exit, not a partial write. drain-signals.js has all-or-nothing tick semantics so it correctly retained all 5 signals. The cost is (a) a burned tick, and (b) any caller that does NOT retain-and-retry silently loses its write. WF-4's stale-age reset declines to fire whenever `git log --since=claimed_at --grep=<task-id>` finds a commit — and commit-convention.md REQUIRES a `Task: <TASK-SLUG>` trailer on any fix/feat delivering a board task, so one commit from the agent before it dies satisfies that grep permanently. Note the irony worth recording: WF-4's own in-file comment names "S2's own outer_claim peer-held check" as the safety net justifying its conservative no-reset — this fix is what removes that safety net. Suggested bound (not prescriptive): increment resume_attempts on the renew branch so WF-3 stays reachable, or cap consecutive renewals, or source liveness from something other than the lock's own presence. Observed 2026-08-25T19:50:53Z: the 19:37Z tick body had already run (commit 39f216d2b at 19:45:48Z — drain complete, 3 agents dispatched and still live). A second delivery of the same cron prompt arrived at 19:50Z; preflight found SF-1 (dev-team-cron-singleton) and the fire-election lock (cron:dev-team:2026-08-25T19:37Z) already held by THIS SAME session, heartbeated both (claimed_at=1787687051, heartbeat_at=1787687364 on both locks — a renewal, not a re-claim after expiry), and returned {"verdict":"RUN","tick":"2026-08-25T19:37Z"} with detail "locks held — continue main.md at gcc-preflight". || WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY A TTL BUG (first read, corrected): the fire-election TTL is 600s against a 1800s cadence, so an expiry-then-reclaim was the obvious hypothesis. The heartbeat_at field falsifies it — the lock never lapsed. The re-entrant RUN is deliberate and has a legitimate purpose: if a tick's body crashes midway, the same-session re-fire must be able to resume rather than strand the tick. || THE ACTUAL GAP: the fire-election lock records that a tick STARTED and is released only at jump:end. It never records how far the body got, so "I hold this tick's lock" is ambiguous between (a) the body crashed, resume it and (b) the body is running fine right now, do not touch it. Both present identically to preflight, and it resolves the ambiguity toward RUN in both cases. A router that trusted the verdict here would have re-run gcc-preflight, re-drained, and re-entered Step 1 / ILC on top of three live agents — the exact duplicate dispatch the fire-election lock exists to prevent. What actually prevented it was out-of-band harness knowledge that the three subagents were still alive, which is NOT available in-flow. || UNTESTED AND IMPORTANT: whether the Phase-B intent gate would have blocked the duplicate spawn depends on whether task_claim treats a re-claim by the SAME owner_client_session as re-entrant (claimed:true) or as held (claimed:false). If re-entrant, the intent locks provide no protection here at all and this is a live duplicate-spawn vector. I did not test it, because the only way to test is to attempt the duplicate claim I am trying to avoid. Worth settling deliberately with a stubbed fixture. || SAME ROOT SHAPE as FIX-DEVTEAM-RESUME-KEY-TTL-3600 (rtr-20260825T1905): a lock's presence or absence being read as a liveness verdict it cannot actually carry. Suggested direction: stamp a completion marker (tick + jump:end reached) into the fire-election lock's payload via task_heartbeat payload_patch as the body advances, so a re-delivery can distinguish resume-after-crash from already-running.

signal_rows.detail: RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING WORK — READ FIRST, this is deliberately NOT a duplicate. review[] row FIX-DRS-CLAIM-TRUSTS-CACHED-DISPATCH-LANE-NOT-EFFECTIVE-NEXT-AGENT (next_agent=qa, updated 2026-08-25T22:33:11Z) already carries, inside its verify_note, a RESIDUAL block naming 3 rows and routing them to 'architect/PO adjudication'. That flag is correct to exist and its instinct to escalate was right. This signal files three corrections to it and does NOT ask for the fix to be reverted. (1) CAUSE IS WRONG, AND THE WRONG CAUSE IMPLIES A FIX THAT DOES NOTHING. The verify_note says the 3 rows diverge 'because the board edit didn't bump updated_at', which implies bumping the board's updated_at would resolve them. It would not. Measured on live data: all 3 rows DO carry a board updated_at (2026-08-25T22:30:08Z on each). What is missing is the DETAIL side. scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq effective_next_agent() takes the board value only inside the conjunct (($board_ts != null) and ($detail_ts != null) and ($board_ts > $detail_ts)); a null $detail_ts makes that conjunct false UNCONDITIONALLY, control falls to the else branch, and $raw_detail_na is returned no matter how fresh the board write is. No board-side bump can make a null detail_ts non-null, so the implied remedy is inert. (2) SCOPE IS 11 ROWS, NOT 3, AND 73 LATENT. Live census of orch-state.json against docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json: 105 detail items carry next_agent, only 32 carry updated_at — 73 (70%) sit in the structurally-unreachable class, so ANY future board next_agent edit on one of them is silently inert too. 15 rows currently diverge. The 4 in review[] carry BOTH timestamps and resolve CORRECTLY by recency (board_ts > detail_ts, board wins) — the comparator itself is sound and must not be 'fixed' blindly. All 11 failures are exactly the detail_ts=null rows: archive/FIX-PRICE-ANOMALY-DISH-SIGNAL-ENVELOPE: board=po IGNORED -> routes architect | backlog/FIX-AUDITOR-B11-NEWS-FRESHNESS-LAYER-SPLIT: board=agent-father IGNORED -> routes ba | backlog/FIX-AUDITOR-TASKBOARD-OVERFLOW-PREDICATE-WIP-ONLY: board=architect IGNORED -> routes ba | backlog/FIX-AUDITOR-HEALTHCHECK-FALSE-UNHEALTHY-NONHTTP-SERVICES: board=dev-mcp-server IGNORED -> routes ba | backlog/FIX-SIGNALQUEUE-DUP-ID-GUARD: board=developer IGNORED -> routes dev | backlog/FIX-AUDITOR-B05-BCTC-FRESHNESS-LAYER-SPLIT: board=agent-father IGNORED -> routes ba | backlog/FIX-ORPHAN-ADOPTION-BOARD-STATE-GUARD: board=pm IGNORED -> routes ba | ready/QA-COWORK-SLOT-SESSION-DOWN-SURVIVAL: board=po IGNORED -> routes qa | ready/FIX-COWORK-LASTFIRED-DECOUPLE-FROM-DELIVERY: board=pm IGNORED -> routes architect | ready/FIX-MACRO-TE-CHROMIUM-FETCH-BROKEN: board=developer IGNORED -> routes architect | ready/FIX-BCTC-BANK-SUMMARY-MAPPING: board=architect IGNORED -> routes ba. (3) VENUE MAKES IT UNACTIONABLE. The residual currently lives only in prose inside a verify_note on a review[] row. Dispatch gates and claim scripts read structured fields, never prose — the same class as feedback_pickers_blind_to_prose_status_note_autoclaim_contraindicated_row, where a do-NOT-build instruction in a status_note was auto-claimed straight through. Parked there it cannot reach whoever routes these rows. WHY AC-4's diff=0 IS NOT EVIDENCE OF CORRECTNESS. The row's AC-4 reports 'dispatch_lane UNCHANGED for all 8 (diff=0)' after re-resolving. That is the EXPECTED output of this defect, not a refutation of it: dispatch_lane was originally stamped from the detail side, and for null-detail_ts rows the resolver deterministically returns the detail side again. The re-resolve reproduced the same answer because the same branch fired both times. diff=0 demonstrates the resolver is deterministic, not that the routing is right. NOTE ON THE CARRIER ROW ITSELF: FIX-DRS-CLAIM-TRUSTS-CACHED-DISPATCH-LANE-NOT-EFFECTIVE-NEXT-AGENT has NO entry at all in backlog-detail.json, so it is itself a member of the unreachable class its own fix was written to address. A router or PO editing .next_agent to redirect any of the 11 therefore produces NO dispatch change, silently. 4 of the 11 are in ready[] and live-dispatchable now; 3 of those carry board_ts=2026-08-25T22:30:08Z, written ~18 minutes before this tick and already inert. CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS (architect's call, explicitly not the router's): (a) treat null detail_ts as infinitely-old so a timestamped board value wins — closest to apparent intent, but flips routing on 11 rows at once and needs a blast-radius review; (b) require detail_ts and fail loudly instead of silently preferring detail; (c) backfill updated_at across the 73 detail items — data-only, leaves the comparator defect latent for the next untimestamped item. Note the 3 ready[] rows ALSO need the separate content call the verify_note already correctly identified (which side is right), and that call is independent of whichever of (a)/(b)/(c) is chosen. NOT MINTING A BOARD ROW: filing for architect triage because (a)/(b)/(c) is a routing-semantics decision with fleet-wide blast radius, and because the adjacent row is still in review[] — minting now risks the duplicate-shipping shape in feedback_po_promote_dedup_blind_to_archived_lane_reships_fixed_work. NOT an AC failure — all 6 ACs verified PASS by the router (fixture 6/6, negative control confirms non-vacuous). This is a new hazard created by the sanctioned design, filed so it is tracked rather than rediscovered.

WHAT LANDED (.claude/skills/dispatch-claim/SKILL.md:702-708):
  # AGE_SEC < CADENCE_SEC — marker IS within the current period (AC-2, no regression).
  if row.owner_client_session not in roster_session_ids:
    continue   # AXIS C / AC-3 — ... treat as abandoned, not live.
roster_session_ids comes from Phase A.5, whose own header (SKILL.md:554,557) reads: "Surface the live cross-team roster ... (advisory; non-blocking)" and is a single task_list_held(kind="session-presence") with NO heartbeat fallback. The diff cites "zero extra round trip" twice as the reason for reusing it — that economy is what selected the weaker oracle.

WHY PRESENCE-ABSENT IS NOT PROOF-OF-DEAD (three independent prior confirmations in this repo):
 (1) feedback_step24_cowork_collision_probe_ttl_exceeds_cadence_daily_false_positive — states the correct staleness oracle for THIS EXACT probe is max(heartbeat_at) across ALL of that session s locks, precisely because absent presence != dead.
 (2) feedback_cron_standalone_step1b1_presence_absence_false_dead_double_arm — presence-ABSENT read as dead produced a DOUBLE ARM in the cron-rearm family. Same oracle, same permissive direction, already burned once.
 (3) feedback_router_almost_rearmed_live_peer_cron_markers_20260822 — presence and heartbeat BOTH misreport for one renewal cadence around a session close; a 2-sample read was needed to disambiguate.

DIRECTION OF FAILURE IS THE POINT. Pre-fix, the bare prefix match blocked unconditionally: over-blocking, whose cost is a skipped slot (recoverable, catch-up exists). Post-fix, Axis C can under-block, whose cost is two dispatchers running the same cowork slot. The published-marker this probe guards exists specifically to stop that; feedback_chef_releases_published_marker_enables_peer_double_publish records the double-publish actually occurring once the marker stopped holding. Axis D does not share this property — it is pure arithmetic on an already-returned claimed_at, no liveness inference.

SCOPE OF EXPOSURE: only the window where a marker is BOTH within its cadence period AND its owner session is momentarily missing from presence — i.e. bounded by one presence-renewal cadence per live dispatcher, not continuous. Small, but it is the exact window a peer tick is most likely to land in, since both sessions fire on the same cron cadence.

CHEAPEST HARDENING (architect s call, not filed as a decision): require BOTH presence-absent AND AGE_SEC > one presence-renewal cadence before skipping — bounds the ambiguity without a second round trip, keeps AC-3 satisfied for genuinely abandoned markers, and costs the truly-dead case only one extra tick of delay. Alternative per (1): max(heartbeat_at) across the owner s locks, which is correct but does add a call.

DO NOT: revert the row or re-open its ACs. Axis D is sound and closes the original 100%-block defect (chef-evening blocked on every fire). Only the Axis C staleness test is in question.

signal_rows.summary: QA-Drain is self-deadlocking. scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq deliberately unions .task_board.done[] into its candidate set (its own line 41), selecting status=="DONE" && effective_next_agent=="qa". scripts/orch-conservation-check.mjs derives LANE_RANK from FLAT_TASK_LANES = [backlog,ready,in_progress,review,qa,done,done_verified], so done(5)->qa(4) is rank-decreasing and scores as a BACKWARD lane move. CONSERVATION_MAX_UNDECLARED_BACKWARD_MOVES defaults to 1, so as soon as TWO done[]-origin rows are eligible the whole orch-apply write ABORTS — taking the legitimately-forward review[]-origin rows in the same batch down with it. The done[] rows can only leave done[] via this drain, so their own presence is what blocks the drain that would clear them. Once done_qa >= 2 the lane is dead until someone intervenes.
signal_rows.action_requested: Resolve the done->qa lane-rank conflict so QA-Drain stops needing a hand-set ORCH_APPLY_DECLARED_BACKWARD_LANE_MOVES. Prefer fix shape 1 or 2; do NOT raise CONSERVATION_MAX_UNDECLARED_BACKWARD_MOVES.
signal_rows.detail:
REPRODUCED LIVE this tick (2026-08-26T03:22Z), then worked around; the underlying conflict is untouched.

THE TWO SHIPPED COMPONENTS DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT `done` MEANS:
 - This board uses done[] = developer-complete, AWAITING QA, and done_verified[] = post-QA terminal.
   Evidence: both blocked rows carry status=DONE AND next_agent=qa. A row that still names qa as its
   next agent is by definition not terminal.
 - orch-conservation-check.mjs:216 + :378 assume the array order IS the pipeline order, so `done`
   ranks ABOVE `qa`. Under that assumption done->qa can only be a regression.
Neither component is individually wrong; the lane vocabulary is. LANE_RANK is a single flat array
reused for a board with TWO terminal lanes and a non-linear DONE->QA->DONE_VERIFIED path.

MEASURED THIS TICK:
  review[] eligible (status=REVIEW, next=qa): 2
  done[]   eligible (status=DONE,   next=qa): 2   <- exceeds the tolerance of 1 by exactly one row
  first attempt: [orch-conservation-check] ABORTED — lane-placement violation: 2 task row(s) moved
                 BACKWARD ... exceeding the tolerated 1 undeclared backward move(s)
  rows drained on that attempt: 0 (of 4 eligible, including 3 P0)
Both done[]-origin rows carry updated_at=2026-08-26T01:23:29Z — the same stamp, i.e. one batch write
earlier tonight created the deadlock. That is why this lane drained normally before today and why the
defect is only now observable.

WHY IT IS A DEADLOCK, NOT A THROTTLE: a done[]-origin row leaves done[] only by being claimed into
qa[] by THIS script. While two or more sit there, every invocation aborts, so none is ever claimed, so
the count never falls back to 1. It is stable at >=2 forever without outside intervention. The blast
radius is the whole batch: review[]-origin rows that move strictly forward are discarded along with it,
so a lane holding 27 review rows drains zero.

THIS TICK S WORKAROUND (explicitly NOT a fix): re-ran with
ORCH_APPLY_DECLARED_BACKWARD_LANE_MOVES set to exactly the two ids, the hatch the guard s own abort
message documents for "this write genuinely intends to move these rows backward on purpose". Intent is
genuine and pre-documented in the claim script, and the declaration was scoped to two named ids after
diffing candidate-vs-live across all seven lanes to confirm nothing ELSE moved non-forward. Batch of 4
then landed (3 P0 + 1 P1), review 29->27, qa 3->7, done 8->6. A router setting a safety-bypass env var
by hand every time the lane is selected is not a durable answer — the next tick, and every peer session,
hits the same wall with no memory of this analysis.

FIX DIRECTION (architect s call, three shapes, ranked):
 1. Teach the lane-placement dimension that done->qa is legitimate when the row carries
    next_agent=="qa" (i.e. exempt the transition the qa-drain script is designed to make). Narrowest,
    keeps the guard fully armed against real stale-revert writes, no vocabulary change.
 2. Have devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq emit the declaration itself for its own done[]-origin picks,
    so the caller never needs the env var. Localizes the knowledge in the component that has the intent.
 3. Split the lane vocabulary so the rank array stops conflating "developer done" with "verified done".
    Correct but far wider blast radius — every consumer of FLAT_TASK_LANES.
Do NOT simply raise CONSERVATION_MAX_UNDECLARED_BACKWARD_MOVES: the tolerance is what catches genuine
stale-full-doc reverts, and raising it to cover N done-origin rows disarms it for exactly the class it
exists to catch.

RELATED, NOT DUPLICATE: feedback_caller_readback_lane_narrower_than_claim_script_silently_kills_lane
records the SECONDARY drain dying on the SAME review-union-done design — there the caller s readback was
narrower than the script s selector; here the conservation guard rejects the union s done-half outright.
Same union, two different consumers, two different silent-death mechanisms. Worth fixing together.

SECOND consumer of "the tick" inside alert-commander derives it differently from the first, and this one is load-bearing for dedup rather than for a cache.

WHAT IS SPECIFIED: docs/agents/alert-commander/flow/stage-dispatch-log.md:96 defines the notebook header as `## c<NNN> · <ISO-timestamp> (slot=<dispatched slot>, tick=<nominal tick>)`, and :39 defines the published-marker gate key as MARKER_KEY="published:alert-commander-market:<nominal_tick>", with <nominal_tick> = "this cycle's dispatched tick". Both want the NOMINAL cron instant.

MEASURED, 3 consecutive cycles (header read from docs/agent-memory/notebooks/alert-commander.md; nominal tick read from this dispatcher's own preflight verdict for the same fire):
  c263 — wall 02:54:46Z, nominal 02:45 → header 02:45. Floored to the 15-min boundary. CORRECT.
  c264 — wall 03:09:45Z, nominal 03:00 → header 03:00. Floored. CORRECT.
  c265 — wall 03:21:45Z, nominal 03:15 → header 03:20. ROUNDED to a 5-min multiple. WRONG.
03:20 is not a cron boundary for this slot (cron is */15 2-8 * * 1-5). It is exactly the key the snapshot lookup uses. So the agent did not merely mis-floor — it appears to have written the SNAPSHOT-lookup key into the field the spec reserves for the NOMINAL tick. Two different "tick" concepts live in this flow with no naming that separates them, and this cycle they cross-contaminated.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE SNAPSHOT ARM: a wrong snapshot key costs a cache miss and falls through to get_cycle_bootstrap — zero data-integrity impact, which is exactly what rtr-20260826T0257-snapshotagentconsumerclock (already drained to architect) documents. A wrong MARKER_KEY is different: the published-marker gate is one of the two mechanisms slot-claim.md names as providing CROSS-TICK dedup (the other is last_fired boundary dedup in cowork-match-slots.js). A marker written under published:alert-commander-market:03:20 does not suppress a later cycle checking published:alert-commander-market:03:15, so the gate silently stops gating. Same failure class as feedback_chef_releases_published_marker_enables_peer_double_publish.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED — limits of this evidence:
  (a) NO damage observed. c265 hit the firing gate and exited silently, and stage-dispatch-log.md:38-39 forbids claiming the marker on a silent-exit cycle, so no marker was written with the bad key. The risk is latent, realised only on a FIRING cycle that mis-derives.
  (b) INTERMITTENT, 1 of 3. Do not model this as deterministic; a fix verified on one cycle proves nothing.
  (c) This is probably a SCOPE GAP, not a regression of the FIX-CHEF-MARKER-KEY-ANCHOR-* rows (all 4 DONE_VERIFIED, correctly). spawn-fanout.md's ANCHOR-3 comment enumerates the slots its SCHEDULED_UTC_LINE was meant to reach — chef-morning/eod/evening, digest-daily, digest-sunday, fb-daily, tnb-audit — and alert-commander is NOT in that list. So the producer half was never intended to serve this agent. Do not reopen the ANCHOR rows on the strength of this.

THE FIX IS ALREADY IN TRANSIT AND STILL DISCARDED: this dispatcher composes SCHEDULED_UTC_LINE into EVERY spawn prompt unconditionally, alert-commander included — the 03:15Z prompt carried the literal line scheduled_utc=2026-08-26T03:15:00.000Z. `grep -rn scheduled_utc docs/agents/alert-commander/` returns ZERO HITS (re-confirmed this tick). The agent is guessing a value it is already being handed. One consumer-side edit — derive nominal_tick from the scheduled_utc line, fall back to floor-to-cron-boundary only when absent — fixes THIS arm and the snapshot arm in rtr-20260826T0257 in the same landing, and needs no producer change.

NOT a duplicate of ARCH-CRON-THREE-TIME-BASES-UNIFY (checked): that SPIKE is about timezone/DST bases across scheduling PLANES (UTC vs Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh vs machine-local France). This is tick-KEY derivation inside a single UTC plane. Archive (docs/data/orch/archive/2026-06.json, 2026-08.json) searched by subject — no prior row.
=== AMENDED 2026-08-26T03:40Z (router, cowork 03:30Z tick) — SECOND OCCURRENCE, CONSECUTIVE. Two corrections to the text above and one new root cause. ===

CORRECTION 1 — limit (b) above UNDERSTATES the frequency. It says "INTERMITTENT, 1 of 3". Measured now over four consecutive cycles:
  c263 — wall 02:54:46Z, nominal 02:45 -> header 02:45. CORRECT (nominal).
  c264 — wall 03:09:45Z, nominal 03:00 -> header 03:00. CORRECT (nominal). Its SNAPSHOT lookup separately used 03:05 — i.e. this cycle held the two values apart correctly.
  c265 — wall 03:21:45Z, nominal 03:15 -> header 03:20. WRONG.
  c266 — wall 03:37:46Z, nominal 03:30 -> header 03:35. WRONG.
So: 2 of 4, and the two failures are CONSECUTIVE, not scattered. Limit (b) as originally written invites treating this as noise. It is not noise — the last two cycles both failed.

CORRECTION 2 — the original text calls the wrong value "ROUNDED to a 5-min multiple". That is imprecise and would send a fixer looking for the wrong arithmetic. c266's wall clock 03:37:46 rounds-to-NEAREST-5 as 03:40, but the header says 03:35. The operation is FLOOR-to-5, and more importantly it is applied to the wall clock AT BOOTSTRAP TIME, not to the notebook-write time.

NEW ROOT CAUSE — a NAME COLLISION across two skill files, which explains why the same agent gets it right some cycles and wrong others:
  .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md Step -1 defines, verbatim:
      TICK = current UTC time formatted as HH:MM (round to nearest 5-min slot, e.g. 02:05 -> "02:05")
      SNAPSHOT_PATH = docs/data/cycle-snapshot-<HH:MM>.json
  docs/agents/alert-commander/flow/stage-dispatch-log.md:39,:96 define MARKER_KEY and the notebook header in terms of <nominal_tick>.
  BOTH quantities are spelled "tick". They are not the same number and never were. On c265 and c266 the header value equals cycle-bootstrap's Step -1 TICK exactly (c265 bootstrap ~03:20 -> 03:20; c266 bootstrap ~03:35 -> 03:35, the file it reported hitting was 55s old at that moment). On c263/c264 the header value equals the nominal cron tick instead. Which of the two identically-named values reaches the header varies per cycle. That is the defect: not bad arithmetic, but two live variables sharing one name across the two files this agent reads every cycle. A fix that only corrects the arithmetic will regress.

EMPIRICAL REFUTATION OF THE OBVIOUS PRODUCER-SIDE FIX — the 03:30Z spawn prompt carried the literal line scheduled_utc=2026-08-26T03:30:00.000Z (this dispatcher composes SCHEDULED_UTC_LINE unconditionally; verified in the prompt it sent). The agent still wrote 03:35. So the value is demonstrably SUPPLIED and IGNORED — not missing. Any fix framed as "start shipping scheduled_utc to alert-commander" is already done and will change nothing. The edit must be consumer-side, inside alert-commander's flow, and should RENAME as well as re-derive so the collision cannot reappear.

INCIDENTAL, bears on the sibling row rtr-20260826T0257-snapshotagentconsumerclock: c266 reported HITTING docs/data/cycle-snapshot-03:34.json. Its own Step -1 rule can only ever compute a 5-minute-multiple path (03:35), so an exact-path lookup could not have found a file named 03:34 — the consumer is evidently not following its own documented exact-match rule either. Note this when landing that row: the consumer's lookup behaviour is itself undocumented, so "fix the name" may not be sufficient on its own. Contrast c265, which DID follow the exact-match rule and therefore missed a snapshot that was 1 minute old.

STILL NOT CLAIMED: no damage yet. c266, like c265, hit the firing gate and exited silently, and stage-dispatch-log.md:38-39 forbids claiming the marker on a silent-exit cycle. The bad key has still never been written. The risk remains latent until a FIRING cycle mis-derives. Limits (a) and (c) above stand unchanged.

=== RETRACTION 2026-08-26T03:55Z (router, cowork 03:45Z tick) — c267 FALSIFIED THE MECHANISM I ASSERTED IN THE 03:40Z AMENDMENT. Read this block before acting on anything above it. ===

Before spawning the 03:45Z cycle I wrote a falsifiable prediction into docs/signals/cowork-team-20260826T034948Z.json: if the floor-5 mechanism claimed above were right, c267 would write tick=03:50. It wrote tick=03:49. The prediction failed and the mechanism is wrong.

WITHDRAWN — three claims, all mine, all refuted by c267:
  (i)  "the operation is FLOOR-to-5 applied to the wall clock at bootstrap" — floor-5 of 03:49:28 is 03:45, not 03:49. FALSE.
  (ii) "the header value equals cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md Step -1's TICK exactly" (round-to-nearest-5) — that yields 03:50 for c267, not 03:49. FALSE. The NAME COLLISION framing built on top of this is therefore UNSUPPORTED as stated and should not be actioned. Two variables named "tick" do genuinely exist across those two files, but the observed wrong value matches NEITHER of them, so the collision is not demonstrated to be the mechanism.
  (iii) from the ORIGINAL filing: "it appears to have written the SNAPSHOT-lookup key into the field the spec reserves for the NOMINAL tick" — c266's snapshot filename was 03:34 while its header said 03:35, so the header is not the snapshot key either. FALSE. c267's header (03:49) equalling its snapshot filename (03:49) is a coincidence of the producer and the consumer landing in the same wall-clock minute.

WHAT SURVIVES — one mechanism, consistent with all three failing cycles. The header equals the agent's OWN RAW WALL CLOCK, HH:MM, at bootstrap time, with no rounding of any kind. Reconstructed from each cycle's snapshot created_at plus the file age the agent itself reported:
  c265 — snapshot 03:19 (created 03:19:29Z) REJECTED by the agent; bootstrap ~03:20 -> header 03:20. nominal 03:15.
  c266 — snapshot 03:34 (created 03:34:39Z) hit at "55s old" -> bootstrap ~03:35 -> header 03:35. nominal 03:30.
  c267 — snapshot 03:49 (created 03:49:15Z) hit at "13s old" -> bootstrap ~03:49:28 -> header 03:49. nominal 03:45.
Three for three. This is plain `date -u +%H:%M` at bootstrap — which is EXACTLY the degraded fallback that spawn-fanout.md's own ANCHOR-3 comment predicts for a worker that does not consume the scheduled_utc line: "emitting nothing lets each worker's own absent-branch fall back to `date -u` exactly as it did before this token existed." alert-commander is outside ANCHOR-3's enumerated slot list, so it was never wired to consume that line, and it is falling back exactly as documented. The defect is a SCOPE GAP, as limit (c) of the original filing already said — that part stands and is now the whole story.

FREQUENCY, corrected again: 3 of 5, and the 3 are CONSECUTIVE (c265, c266, c267). The 03:40Z amendment said 2 of 4. The original filing said 1 of 3. It has been wrong on every cycle since it started and has not self-corrected.

STILL UNEXPLAINED, stated as an open question rather than guessed at: c263 (wall ~02:52, header 02:45) and c264 (wall ~03:06, header 03:00) wrote the NOMINAL tick correctly, which the raw-wall-clock mechanism does not account for. I do not have a mechanism for that and am not going to invent one — two failed hypotheses in two ticks is enough. Whoever lands this should treat "why did c263/c264 get it right" as a real question, because the answer determines whether the fix is "start consuming scheduled_utc" or "stop an existing correct path from being bypassed".

UNCHANGED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING: scheduled_utc was supplied in the spawn prompt on ALL THREE failing cycles (03:15/03:30/03:45, composed unconditionally by this dispatcher) and ignored every time; `grep -rn scheduled_utc docs/agents/alert-commander/` is still ZERO HITS. No damage yet — all three failing cycles exited silently and stage-dispatch-log.md:38-39 forbids claiming the marker on a silent exit, so the bad key has still never been written. The consequence argument in the original filing (MARKER_KEY is one of two cross-tick dedup mechanisms per slot-claim.md, so a mis-derived key silently stops the gate gating) is unaffected by this retraction — only the mechanism was wrong, not the impact.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC: elapsed time IS the severity argument for a STALE-class finding. A dev-team reader triaging 'outcome evaluation stalled 2+ days' schedules it behind other work; the same reader seeing 'stalled 31 days' treats it as a dead job. WHY THE EXISTING GUARDS DID NOT CATCH IT: NO HALLUCINATED COUNTS binds only the four canonical counts from db-integrity-counts.sh (ohlc_violations_count, scale_gt100x_count, vnindex_cache_rows_count, low_confidence_reports_count) — an age in a .detail string is outside its scope. NO FABRICATED SCOPE CLAIMS binds only date-SCOPE claims about the OHLC residue, checked against ohlc_violation_distinct_dates. Neither covers a derived age. So this is a genuine uncovered surface, not a repeat violation of a rule already in force.

MECHANISM: effective_depends_on() unions .depends_on + .depends + .blocked_by (eligibility lib :232), and deps_satisfied() passes when all resolve DONE_VERIFIED — including via archive_status_map(), which was added precisely so cold-eviction would stop manufacturing false blocks (FIX-DEPSSATISFIED-COLD-ARCHIVED-DEP-RESOLVES-MISSING). That half works. The unfixed half is that the row own .status was set to BLOCKED when the block was created and nothing clears it when the blocker completes. Because :117/:160 filter on status BEFORE deps are evaluated, a row can be simultaneously deps-satisfied and permanently unpickable.

WHY IT IS NOT SELF-HEALING: the only writer that would clear the status is whoever closes the BLOCKER row, and that agent has no reason to scan for downstream rows naming it. So the stale flag survives every tick indefinitely.

SCOPE NOTE / DO NOT DOUBLE-COUNT: two of the four (FIX-ORCHSTATE-HOTFILE-BLOAT..., FU-CHEF-MARKER-INFLOW) ALSO have next_agent unset, which is a separate already-filed defect (CLEAN-ORCHSTATE-DUP-ROWS-NULL-NEXTAGENT-UNSPAWNABLE-READY-SLOTS / FIX-TASKSCHEMA-NEXTAGENT-CONDITIONAL-MANDATORY). TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-9 (P0) and VERIFY-FIX-COVERAGE-SWEEP (P1) have next_agent set and would become dispatchable immediately.

DELIBERATELY NOT SELF-ACTUATED: the router did not flip these four statuses. Auto-clearing a BLOCKED flag without reading each row prose is exactly the shape that once auto-claimed a contraindicated do-NOT-build row. Each of the four needs its prose read before it is released — that is a PO call, not a bookkeeping edit.

### Why this is worse than a wrong number

The cron's own NO TREND NARRATION clause states that the count-over-time comparison "is read
DETERMINISTICALLY from the history's `counts` fields by the router/dev-team, not editorialized by
you." That defence works for the four canonical counts. It does not work here, because:

  - `counts` carries ONLY ohlc_violations / scale_gt100x / vnindex_cache_rows /
    low_confidence_reports. Neither cron_job_runs nor deep_fetch nor fred_series has a field there.
  - A REAL finding that VANISHES from `findings[]` is therefore invisible to the deterministic
    reader — and to any reader, human or script, an absent finding reads as resolved.
  - Nothing in the entry distinguishes "checked, still broken" from "not checked this cycle" from
    "checked and re-classified by-design". All three render identically: absent.

### This is the coverage-is-a-set defect, one layer down

R-5 was written because `tables_checked=14` passed a non-null check while the mandated set was 17,
and the shrink hid a CRITICAL and a HIGH. R-5 fixed that — but it binds which tables get CHECKED.
Nothing binds which get RECORDED. `tables_checked: 17` is still a scalar, and it reads 17 whether
the entry carries 17 dispositions or 4. The same defect shape, at the next level down, undetected
by the guard written for the level above.

### Remedy shape (for whoever owns the schema)

The entry needs a per-table DISPOSITION MAP covering all 17 names — each with
`{checked: bool, verdict, severity, signal_id}` — not a `findings[]` subset plus a scalar count.
Then "absent" becomes structurally impossible and "clean" has to be asserted explicitly per table.

During the go:embed prose extraction, intermediate commit 928557a66 stripped Vietnamese diacritics from all 64 MarketTrendLabel entries (THUAN LOI for THUẬN LỢI etc). Fixed in 88e93338f, so HEAD is correct and this is NOT an open data defect. The defect is in the DETECTOR.

The full suite passed green on the broken commit. Root cause is structural, not a near-miss:

1. TestQueReferenceHexagram1Snapshot (hexagram_invariant_test.go:296) is the only content-fidelity test in the package. It pins exactly two fields, CoreMeaning.En and Phases[0].Gloss.En, on hexagram 1 only. Both are ENGLISH. It is blind to Vietnamese corruption on every hexagram including the one it covers.

2. All 7 invariant tests assert emptiness and cardinality only (is empty / got %d want 64). Diacritic stripping preserves non-emptiness and preserves count 64, so every assertion holds.

3. grep for any accented literal or MarketTrendLabel across all *_test.go in the package returns ZERO hits. No test anywhere pins an accented string.

Generalization worth checking: the suite snapshot-tests the .En half of localized fields and leaves the .Vi half entirely unasserted. For a service whose product IS Vietnamese-localized prose, the tested half is the half nobody ships. Any content regression confined to Vietnamese text is invisible to CI by construction.

qa demonstrated this empirically via a worktree diff at the broken commit and correctly reported it as a finding rather than a blocker (the fix had already landed). Logging works in the container generally (3895 lines). This ONE module emits nothing. Among the silent calls is logger.info at ocr_worker.py:199 on the main OCR entry path, which should fire on every invocation, so this is not a rare-branch artifact.

WHAT IT BLOCKS. The standing goal is to replace tesseract with PaddleOCR to IMPROVE BCTC extraction quality. Quality improvement is a measured claim. With this module dark there is no denominator: we cannot count how often the rescue fires, cannot compare per-page char yield tesseract vs paddle, and cannot detect the budget-exhaustion warning at :509 that the code itself added precisely so a page silently reverting to a weak read would be VISIBLE. CORRECTS AN EARLIER ROUTER CLAIM. Router previously recorded that mechanism B (ocr_worker page-rescue, PaddleOCR lang=vi, ungated) RUNS in production today. Code-reachability remains true: grep -c OCR_TEXT_BACKEND ocr_worker.py = 0, so nothing gates it. But there is NO execution evidence, and this defect means there CANNOT be. The honest state is reachable and ungated, firing rate UNKNOWN and currently unknowable. Distinguish reachable from observed. The code-in-image is not branch-executes lesson applies to the router own earlier conclusion here.

NOTE the 4 paddle hits that DO appear in docker logs are all pek_engine_adapter (PP-StructureV2 table mode, mechanism A, PID 1). Mechanism A is observable; mechanism B is not. Do NOT read mechanism A log lines as evidence about mechanism B. That exact conflation invalidated an earlier analysis.

signal_rows.summary: Decision-journal cap-roll is a lost-update race. When a journal breaches its byte cap, every concurrent agent independently computes the SAME next continuation filename and creates it with Write() (whole-file), so the later writer silently clobbers the earlier one's entry. Two qa sessions hit this within 60 seconds today on sprint-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP-qa-31.md. Data was recovered only because the second agent happened to notice.
signal_rows.action_requested: Mint a row to make the cap-roll safe under concurrency. The existing fleet rule 'notebooks must be appended with plain printf >>, never Edit/Write' already encodes the correct discipline but is scoped to NOTEBOOKS; decision journals under docs/agent-memory/decisions/ are governed by a separate cap-roll procedure that mandates creating a new file, which is precisely the unsafe operation. Options for the implementer: append-only creation (printf >> against the continuation path, which is safe because it merges rather than replaces), or a session-unique continuation suffix, or taking the git commit-mutex across the roll.
signal_rows.detail:
ROUTER-VERIFIED ON DISK AND IN GIT, not merely reported by the agent.

WHAT HAPPENED. sprint-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP-qa-30.md breached its 36000B byte cap (final 37591B / 146L). Two qa sessions from the same 4-row drain batch reached their cap check within about a minute of each other. Both computed the next continuation name as ...-qa-31.md. The vndirect session created it and wrote STEP qa-S242. The DRS session then created the same path with Write(), which is whole-file and does not merge, clobbering qa-S242.

WHY IT WAS CAUGHT. The DRS agent noticed the collision, recovered the peer's entry verbatim from that peer's still-intact notebook (a second, independent copy of the same content), and reinserted it chronologically ahead of its own. Router confirmed the final state: qa-31.md now holds STEP qa-S242 (10:58Z, vndirect) at line 9 and STEP qa-S243 (10:59Z, DRS) at line 20, correct order, and both strings present.

WHY THIS IS STILL HIGH SEVERITY DESPITE THE CLEAN OUTCOME. The recovery depended on two pieces of luck, not on any mechanism. First, the clobbered content happened to be duplicated in the peer's notebook, so a source existed to recover FROM; a journal-only entry would have been unrecoverable. Second, the clobbering agent happened to look. Nothing in the roll procedure detects the collision, and git did not catch it either -- the peer had already committed 18d1f2717 before the clobber, so the working-tree loss would have surfaced as a silent content deletion inside the next commit, not as a conflict. Explicit pathspec would not have helped: this is one file, one path, two writers.

BLAST RADIUS. Any capped shared journal under a multi-agent batch. Today's 4-row qa-drain fan-out is exactly the shape that produces it: N agents, one sprint, one shared journal, one shared cap. It is more likely, not less, as batch sizes grow -- the QA-drain take budget is currently capped at 10.

NOTE ON THE ADJACENT RULE. The fleet already knows this failure mode: notebooks are required to be appended with printf >> precisely to avoid whole-file replacement under concurrency. The decision-journal roll path appears to have been written without inheriting that constraint, so the lesson is enforced on one artifact class and not on the neighbouring one.

Step 2.4 Axis D age-bound fails to clear a structurally-prior-period marker when the prior fire ran later-in-day than the current dispatch. Live case 2026-08-26T19:47:35Z, hand-dispatch of chef-evening: held row published:chef-evening:2026-08-25 (period key = YESTERDAY) had claimed_at=1787687605 (2026-08-25T19:53:25Z), AGE_SEC=86050 < CADENCE_SEC=86400, so Axis D took the CURRENT-PERIOD branch and did not `continue`. Root cause: AGE_SEC is arithmetic on claimed_at, which only tracks the period boundary if each fire claims at a non-decreasing time-of-day; yesterdays chef-evening claimed at 19:53:25Z (8m late vs the 45 19 cron) while todays dispatch ran at 19:47Z, opening a 5m50s band in which a prior-period marker reads as current. Band width = (prior claim lateness) - (current dispatch lateness); recurs on any slot whose fire jitter varies, daily 86400s and weekly 604800s alike. Axis C would have cleared it, but only via the known-bad path (roster holds dispatcher sessions, markers are held by agent sessions - see feedback_router_hand_dispatch_double_fires_guaranteed_slot, false-clears 7/7), so the two axes disagree and neither is sound here. Cheap direction (PO to rule): compare the period-key SUFFIX already embedded in the task_id against the slots own publish_date_basis, instead of (or as a guard on) pure claimed_at arithmetic - the string `2026-08-25` is unambiguous where the age is not. This dispatch was correctly suppressed anyway, but by ps-grep evidence (live pid 70235 running the slot), NOT by Axis D - the axis was right by coincidence, and the same band inverts to a FALSE-CLEAR whenever the current fire runs later-in-day than the prior one.
